description: Question bank based on 'Major Geographical Features' study notes for FDA/SDA competitive examination. Comprehensive coverage of all sections.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the major divisions of the ocean floor in a simplified cross-section?

options.A: Continental shelf, continental slope, continental rise and deep-ocean basin
options.B: Continental shelf, abyssal plain, mid-oceanic ridge and trench
options.C: Continental slope, seamount, guyot and fracture zone
options.D: Continental rise, submarine fan, atoll and lagoon

questions.explanation: A simplified cross-section includes the continental shelf, continental slope, continental rise and deep-ocean basin. The deep-ocean basin includes features such as abyssal plains, trenches and mid-oceanic ridges.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a continental margin?

options.A: The submerged outer edge of a continent, extending from the shoreline to the deep ocean floor
options.B: The deepest part of the ocean floor
options.C: A chain of underwater mountains formed at divergent boundaries
options.D: A flat region of the deep-ocean floor

questions.explanation: A continental margin is the submerged outer edge of a continent, extending from the shoreline to the deep ocean floor. It includes the continental shelf, continental slope and, where developed, the continental rise.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following best describes an active continental margin?

options.A: It lies near an active plate boundary and commonly has earthquakes, volcanism, trenches or a narrow shelf
options.B: It is generally farther from a plate boundary and often has a broad shelf and thick sediment accumulation
options.C: It is formed by the accumulation of sediments transported by turbidity currents
options.D: It is a broad, gently sloping accumulation of sediment at the base of a continental slope

questions.explanation: An active margin lies near an active plate boundary and commonly has earthquakes, volcanism, trenches or a narrow shelf. A passive margin is generally farther from a plate boundary and often has a broad shelf and thick sediment accumulation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following best describes a passive continental margin?

options.A: It lies near an active plate boundary and commonly has earthquakes, volcanism and trenches
options.B: It is generally farther from a plate boundary and often has a broad shelf and thick sediment accumulation
options.C: It is a narrow, deep depression in the ocean floor formed at a convergent plate boundary
options.D: It is a long underwater mountain chain formed at a divergent plate boundary

questions.explanation: A passive margin is generally farther from a plate boundary and often has a broad shelf and thick sediment accumulation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a continental shelf?

options.A: A gently sloping, submerged extension of a continent that stretches from the shoreline to the shelf break
options.B: The relatively steep submarine slope extending from the shelf break down towards the deep-ocean floor
options.C: A broad, gently sloping accumulation of sediment at the base of a continental slope
options.D: A long, narrow, very deep depression in the ocean floor

questions.explanation: A continental shelf is a gently sloping, submerged extension of a continent that stretches from the shoreline to the shelf break, where the seabed descends more steeply into the continental slope.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the shelf break?

options.A: The point or zone where the gentle continental shelf transitions into the steeper continental slope
options.B: The deepest part of the ocean trench
options.C: The central rift valley of a mid-oceanic ridge
options.D: The flat region of the abyssal plain

questions.explanation: The shelf break is the point or zone where the gentle continental shelf transitions into the steeper continental slope. Its depth is commonly around 100-200 metres, but it varies considerably.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the commonly quoted global average width of a continental shelf?

options.A: Roughly 10-20 kilometres

questions.explanation: There is no fixed width. Shelves range from very narrow to hundreds of kilometres wide; a commonly quoted global average is roughly 70-80 kilometres.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a main characteristic of continental shelves?

options.A: They are relatively shallow, gently sloping, submerged parts of continents
options.B: They are the steepest parts of the ocean floor
options.C: They are the deepest parts of the ocean floor
options.D: They are formed only at convergent plate boundaries

questions.explanation: Continental shelves are relatively shallow, gently sloping, submerged parts of continents; receive substantial sunlight in many areas; and often support productive fisheries and important oil, gas and mineral resources.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are continental shelves economically important?

options.A: They support fisheries, offshore petroleum and natural-gas extraction, marine transport, seabed minerals, renewable-energy installations and coastal ecosystems
options.B: They are the deepest parts of the ocean and contain valuable minerals
options.C: They are formed by subduction and contain valuable volcanic materials
options.D: They are the longest mountain chains on Earth

questions.explanation: Continental shelves support fisheries, offshore petroleum and natural-gas extraction, marine transport, seabed minerals, renewable-energy installations and coastal ecosystems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are continental shelves often rich fishing grounds?

options.A: Shallow water allows sunlight to support photosynthesis, while nutrient supply from mixing, upwelling and river inputs can sustain plankton and food webs
options.B: They are the deepest parts of the ocean and contain large fish
options.C: They are formed by subduction and contain volcanic nutrients
options.D: They are the longest mountain chains on Earth

questions.explanation: Shallow water allows sunlight to support photosynthesis, while nutrient supply from mixing, upwelling and river inputs can sustain plankton and food webs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where is a broad continental shelf found in India?

options.A: The western continental margin of India, particularly off parts of Gujarat and the west coast
options.B: The eastern continental margin of India, particularly off the Coromandel coast

questions.explanation: The western continental margin of India has a relatively broad shelf in several sectors, particularly off parts of Gujarat and the west coast. Shelf width varies by location.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between a continental shelf and a continental slope?

options.A: The shelf is a shallow, gently inclined submerged extension of the continent; the slope is the steeper descent from the shelf break towards the deep ocean
options.B: The shelf is the steepest part of the ocean floor; the slope is the shallowest part
options.C: The shelf is formed by subduction; the slope is formed by seafloor spreading
options.D: The shelf is a deep-ocean floor feature; the slope is a continental feature

questions.explanation: The shelf is a shallow, gently inclined submerged extension of the continent; the slope is the steeper descent from the shelf break towards the deep ocean.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a continental slope?

options.A: The relatively steep submarine slope extending from the shelf break down towards the deep-ocean floor or continental rise
options.B: A gently sloping, submerged extension of a continent
options.C: A broad, gently sloping accumulation of sediment at the base of a continental slope
options.D: A long, narrow, very deep depression in the ocean floor

questions.explanation: A continental slope is the relatively steep submarine slope extending from the shelf break down towards the deep-ocean floor or continental rise.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of continental slopes?

options.A: They have a much steeper gradient than shelves, may be cut by submarine canyons, and commonly mark the transition from continental crust to oceanic crust
options.B: They are extremely flat and gently sloping regions of the deep-ocean floor
options.C: They are long, narrow, very deep depressions formed at convergent boundaries
options.D: They are underwater mountain chains formed at divergent boundaries

questions.explanation: Continental slopes have a much steeper gradient than shelves, may be cut by submarine canyons, and commonly mark the transition from continental crust to oceanic crust.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the typical average gradient of a continental slope?

options.A: A few degrees, though local slopes can be much steeper

questions.explanation: The average gradient of a continental slope varies widely, but commonly lies in the range of a few degrees; local slopes can be much steeper.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are submarine canyons?

options.A: Deep, steep-sided valleys cut into the continental shelf and slope, often associated with sediment-laden turbidity currents and submarine mass movements
options.B: Long, narrow, very deep depressions formed at subduction zones
options.C: Underwater mountain chains formed at divergent boundaries
options.D: Broad, flat regions of the deep-ocean floor

questions.explanation: Submarine canyons are deep, steep-sided valleys cut into the continental shelf and slope, often associated with sediment-laden turbidity currents and submarine mass movements.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a turbidity current?

options.A: A dense, sediment-laden current that flows downslope under gravity along the seabed, capable of transporting large quantities of sediment
options.B: A warm ocean current that flows along the surface
options.C: A current formed by wind action on the ocean surface
options.D: A current formed by tidal forces in estuaries

questions.explanation: A turbidity current is a dense, sediment-laden current that flows downslope under gravity along the seabed, capable of transporting large quantities of sediment.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main function of submarine canyons in sediment transfer?

options.A: They can channel sediments from continental shelves and slopes to deep-sea fans and the deep-ocean basin
options.B: They prevent sediment from reaching the deep ocean
options.D: They form abyssal plains by depositing coarse gravel

questions.explanation: Submarine canyons can channel sediments from continental shelves and slopes to deep-sea fans and the deep-ocean basin.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a continental rise?

options.A: A broad, gently sloping accumulation of sediment at the base of a continental slope, where the steep slope grades into the deep-ocean floor
options.B: A gently sloping, submerged extension of a continent
options.C: The relatively steep submarine slope extending from the shelf break
options.D: A long, narrow, very deep depression in the ocean floor

questions.explanation: A continental rise is a broad, gently sloping accumulation of sediment at the base of a continental slope, where the steep slope grades into the deep-ocean floor.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How is a continental rise formed?

options.A: It commonly forms through the accumulation of sediments transported downslope by turbidity currents, submarine landslides and other mass-flow processes
options.B: It forms through seafloor spreading at divergent boundaries
options.C: It forms through subduction of oceanic lithosphere
options.D: It forms through wind deposition of sand

questions.explanation: A continental rise commonly forms through the accumulation of sediments transported downslope by turbidity currents, submarine landslides and other mass-flow processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where is the continental rise best developed?

options.A: It is generally well developed along many passive continental margins; it may be narrow, poorly developed or absent along active margins where trenches occur
options.B: It is best developed along active continental margins where trenches occur
options.C: It is best developed in the central rift valley of mid-oceanic ridges
options.D: It is best developed on abyssal plains

questions.explanation: The continental rise is generally well developed along many passive continental margins; it may be narrow, poorly developed or absent along active margins where trenches occur.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a submarine fan?

options.A: A fan-shaped sediment accumulation at the foot of a submarine canyon or slope, built by sediment-laden flows
options.B: A long, narrow, very deep depression in the ocean floor
options.C: An underwater mountain chain formed at a divergent boundary
options.D: A broad, extremely flat region of the deep-ocean floor

questions.explanation: A submarine fan is a fan-shaped sediment accumulation at the foot of a submarine canyon or slope, built by sediment-laden flows. Large examples are called deep-sea fans.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does a continental rise differ from a continental slope?

options.A: The slope is the steep descent from the shelf; the rise is the gentler sediment-built zone at the slope's base
options.B: The slope is the gentler sediment-built zone; the rise is the steep descent from the shelf
options.C: The slope is a deep-ocean floor feature; the rise is a continental feature
options.D: The slope is formed by seafloor spreading; the rise is formed by subduction

questions.explanation: The slope is the steep descent from the shelf; the rise is the gentler sediment-built zone at the slope's base.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an ocean basin?

options.A: A vast depression in the Earth's crust occupied by ocean water and underlain mainly by oceanic crust, including the deep-ocean floor and its relief features
options.B: A shallow submerged extension of a continent
options.C: A long, narrow, very deep depression formed at a convergent boundary
options.D: A long underwater mountain chain formed at a divergent boundary

questions.explanation: An ocean basin is a vast depression in the Earth's crust occupied by ocean water and underlain mainly by oceanic crust, including the deep-ocean floor and its relief features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the major ocean basins?

options.A: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic ocean basins
options.B: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Mediterranean and Arctic ocean basins
options.C: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Antarctic ocean basins
options.D: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Caribbean ocean basins

questions.explanation: The major ocean basins are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic ocean basins.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a major feature of ocean basins?

options.A: Abyssal plains, mid-ocean ridges, ocean trenches, seamounts, guyots, fracture zones, submarine plateaus and deep-sea fans
options.B: Continental shelves, continental slopes, continental rises and shelf breaks

questions.explanation: The major features of ocean basins include abyssal plains, mid-ocean ridges, ocean trenches, seamounts, guyots, fracture zones, submarine plateaus and deep-sea fans.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How are ocean basins formed and modified?

options.A: They are created and reshaped by plate tectonics, seafloor spreading, subduction, volcanism, faulting, sedimentation and changes in sea level
options.B: They are created only by river erosion
options.C: They are created only by wind deposition
options.D: They are created only by glacial erosion

questions.explanation: Ocean basins are created and reshaped by plate tectonics, seafloor spreading, subduction, volcanism, faulting, sedimentation and changes in sea level.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is oceanic crust mainly composed of?

options.A: It is predominantly basaltic to gabbroic in composition and is generally thinner and denser than continental crust
options.B: It is predominantly granitic in composition and is generally thicker and less dense than continental crust
options.C: It is predominantly sedimentary in composition and is generally thicker than continental crust
options.D: It is predominantly metamorphic in composition and is generally thinner than continental crust

questions.explanation: Oceanic crust is predominantly basaltic to gabbroic in composition and is generally thinner and denser than continental crust.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an abyssal plain?

options.A: A very broad, extremely flat or gently sloping region of the deep-ocean floor, commonly lying at depths of roughly 3,000-6,000 metres
options.B: A gently sloping, submerged extension of a continent
options.C: A long, narrow, very deep depression formed at a convergent boundary
options.D: An underwater mountain chain formed at a divergent boundary

questions.explanation: An abyssal plain is a very broad, extremely flat or gently sloping region of the deep-ocean floor, commonly lying at depths of roughly 3,000-6,000 metres.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How are abyssal plains formed?

options.A: Fine sediments, including clay and the remains of microscopic marine organisms, gradually accumulate and bury irregular oceanic crust and volcanic relief
options.B: They are formed by seafloor spreading at divergent boundaries
options.C: They are formed by subduction of oceanic lithosphere
options.D: They are formed by wind deposition of sand

questions.explanation: Fine sediments, including clay and the remains of microscopic marine organisms, gradually accumulate and bury irregular oceanic crust and volcanic relief.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are abyssal plains among the flattest regions on Earth?

options.A: Long-term accumulation of fine-grained sediments smooths and fills depressions in the underlying ocean floor
options.B: They are formed by volcanic eruptions that create perfectly flat surfaces
options.C: They are formed by glacial erosion that levels the ocean floor
options.D: They are formed by wind erosion that flattens the ocean floor

questions.explanation: Long-term accumulation of fine-grained sediments smooths and fills depressions in the underlying ocean floor, making abyssal plains among the flattest regions on Earth.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are main characteristics of abyssal plains?

options.A: Great depth, very low gradient, extensive area, darkness, cold water and high pressure
options.B: Shallow depth, steep gradient, small area and abundant sunlight
options.C: Moderate depth, moderate gradient and warm water
options.D: Variable depth, steep gradient and strong tidal influence

questions.explanation: The main characteristics of abyssal plains are great depth, very low gradient, extensive area, darkness, cold water and high pressure.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where are abyssal plains found?

options.A: They occur in the deep Atlantic, Indian and Pacific oceans, particularly where sediment supply is sufficient to bury rough basement topography
options.B: They occur only in the Arctic Ocean
options.C: They occur only in the Southern Ocean
options.D: They occur only in the Mediterranean Sea

questions.explanation: Abyssal plains occur in the deep Atlantic, Indian and Pacific oceans, particularly where sediment supply is sufficient to bury rough basement topography.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between an abyssal plain and a continental shelf?

options.A: An abyssal plain is a deep-ocean-floor feature several kilometres below sea level; a continental shelf is a shallow submerged extension of a continent
options.B: An abyssal plain is a shallow submerged extension of a continent; a continental shelf is a deep-ocean-floor feature
options.C: An abyssal plain is a long, narrow, very deep depression; a continental shelf is a broad, flat region
options.D: An abyssal plain is formed by subduction; a continental shelf is formed by seafloor spreading

questions.explanation: An abyssal plain is a deep-ocean-floor feature several kilometres below sea level; a continental shelf is a shallow submerged extension of a continent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an ocean trench?

options.A: A long, narrow, very deep depression in the ocean floor, generally formed at a convergent plate boundary where one tectonic plate subducts beneath another
options.B: A very broad, extremely flat region of the deep-ocean floor
options.C: A long underwater mountain chain formed at a divergent plate boundary
options.D: A gently sloping, submerged extension of a continent

questions.explanation: An ocean trench is a long, narrow, very deep depression in the ocean floor, generally formed at a convergent plate boundary where one tectonic plate subducts beneath another.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How are ocean trenches formed?

options.A: As a dense oceanic lithospheric plate bends and descends into the mantle at a subduction zone, it creates a deep trench near the plate boundary
options.B: As plates diverge, mantle material rises and partially melts, creating a deep trench
options.C: As wind erodes the ocean floor, it creates a deep trench
options.D: As rivers cut into the ocean floor, they create a deep trench

questions.explanation: As a dense oceanic lithospheric plate bends and descends into the mantle at a subduction zone, it creates a deep trench near the plate boundary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are characteristics of ocean trenches?

options.A: They are narrow, elongated, extremely deep features, commonly associated with earthquakes, subduction, volcanic arcs and deep-sea ecosystems
options.B: They are broad, flat, shallow features with abundant sunlight
options.C: They are formed at divergent boundaries where new crust is created
options.D: They are gently sloping, sediment-built zones at the base of continental slopes

questions.explanation: Ocean trenches are narrow, elongated, extremely deep features, commonly associated with earthquakes, subduction, volcanic arcs and deep-sea ecosystems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the deepest known ocean trench?

options.A: The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific
options.B: The Tonga Trench in the southwestern Pacific
options.C: The Puerto Rico Trench in the Atlantic Ocean
options.D: The Java Trench in the Indian Ocean

questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific is the deepest known ocean trench. Challenger Deep is its deepest surveyed area, with measured depth estimates around 10.9 kilometres; values vary by survey and method.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is Challenger Deep?

options.A: The deepest surveyed area of the Mariana Trench
options.C: A major section of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge
options.D: A large submarine fan in the Pacific Ocean

questions.explanation: Challenger Deep is the deepest surveyed area of the Mariana Trench, with measured depth estimates around 10.9 kilometres; values vary by survey and method.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are other major ocean trenches?

options.A: Tonga, Philippine, Japan, Kuril-Kamchatka, Peru-Chile and Puerto Rico trenches
options.B: Mariana, Mid-Atlantic, East Pacific Rise and Indian Ridge
options.C: Grand Canyon, Kali Gandaki and Sundarbans

questions.explanation: Other major ocean trenches include the Tonga, Philippine, Japan, Kuril-Kamchatka, Peru-Chile and Puerto Rico trenches.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are other major ocean trenches?

options.A: Tonga, Philippine, Japan, Kuril-Kamchatka, Peru-Chile and Puerto Rico trenches
options.B: Mariana, Mid-Atlantic, East Pacific Rise and Indian Ridge
options.C: Grand Canyon, Kali Gandaki and Sundarbans

questions.explanation: Other major ocean trenches include the Tonga, Philippine, Japan, Kuril-Kamchatka, Peru-Chile and Puerto Rico trenches.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are trenches associated with earthquakes?

options.A: Subduction zones generate earthquakes as plates interact, lock, slip and deform; the largest earthquakes can occur along the plate interface
options.B: Trenches are formed by wind erosion, which causes earthquakes
options.C: Trenches are formed by river erosion, which causes earthquakes
options.D: Trenches are formed by glacial activity, which causes earthquakes

questions.explanation: Subduction zones generate earthquakes as plates interact, lock, slip and deform. The largest earthquakes can occur along the plate interface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between an ocean trench and an abyssal plain?

options.A: A trench is a narrow, very deep depression associated mainly with subduction; an abyssal plain is a broad, relatively flat deep-ocean region
options.B: A trench is a broad, relatively flat deep-ocean region; an abyssal plain is a narrow, very deep depression
options.C: A trench is formed at a divergent boundary; an abyssal plain is formed at a convergent boundary
options.D: A trench is a shallow submerged extension of a continent; an abyssal plain is a deep-ocean-floor feature

questions.explanation: A trench is a narrow, very deep depression associated mainly with subduction; an abyssal plain is a broad, relatively flat deep-ocean region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a mid-oceanic ridge?

options.A: A long underwater mountain chain formed mainly at divergent plate boundaries where tectonic plates move apart and new oceanic crust is produced
options.B: A long, narrow, very deep depression formed at a convergent plate boundary
options.C: A very broad, extremely flat region of the deep-ocean floor
options.D: A gently sloping, submerged extension of a continent

questions.explanation: A mid-oceanic ridge is a long underwater mountain chain formed mainly at divergent plate boundaries where tectonic plates move apart and new oceanic crust is produced.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How are mid-oceanic ridges formed?

options.A: As plates diverge, mantle material rises and partially melts due to decompression; magma cools to form new oceanic crust, creating an elevated ridge system
options.B: As plates converge, one plate subducts beneath another, creating an elevated ridge system
options.C: As wind erodes the ocean floor, it creates an elevated ridge system
options.D: As rivers deposit sediment, they create an elevated ridge system

questions.explanation: As plates diverge, mantle material rises and partially melts due to decompression. Magma cools to form new oceanic crust, creating an elevated ridge system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is seafloor spreading?

options.A: The process by which new oceanic lithosphere forms at mid-ocean ridges and moves outward on both sides as plates separate
options.B: The process by which oceanic lithosphere is destroyed at ocean trenches
options.C: The process by which continents move across the ocean floor
options.D: The process by which wind deposits sand on the ocean floor

questions.explanation: Seafloor spreading is the process by which new oceanic lithosphere forms at mid-ocean ridges and moves outward on both sides as plates separate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are characteristics of mid-ocean ridges?

options.A: They form a globally connected submarine mountain system, commonly have a central rift valley in slow-spreading sections, experience volcanic activity and shallow earthquakes, and are sites of hydrothermal vents
options.B: They are narrow, elongated, extremely deep features associated with deep earthquakes and subduction
options.C: They are broad, extremely flat regions with very low gradient and high pressure
options.D: They are gently sloping, sediment-built zones at the base of continental slopes

questions.explanation: Mid-ocean ridges form a globally connected submarine mountain system, commonly have a central rift valley in slow-spreading sections, experience volcanic activity and shallow earthquakes, and are sites of hydrothermal vents.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the longest mountain chain on Earth?

options.A: The global mid-ocean ridge system

questions.explanation: The global mid-ocean ridge system is the longest mountain chain on Earth, extending for tens of thousands of kilometres beneath the oceans.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Mid-Atlantic Ridge?

options.A: A major section of the global mid-ocean ridge system running through the Atlantic Ocean, separating the American plates from the Eurasian and African plates in different segments
options.B: A long, narrow, very deep depression in the Atlantic Ocean
options.C: A broad, extremely flat region of the Atlantic Ocean floor
options.D: A gently sloping, submerged extension of the North American continent

questions.explanation: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is a major section of the global mid-ocean ridge system running through the Atlantic Ocean, separating the American plates from the Eurasian and African plates in different segments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between a mid-ocean ridge and an ocean trench?

options.A: A ridge forms at a divergent boundary where new oceanic crust is created; a trench forms at a convergent boundary where oceanic lithosphere is subducted
options.B: A ridge forms at a convergent boundary where oceanic lithosphere is subducted; a trench forms at a divergent boundary where new oceanic crust is created
options.C: A ridge is a broad, flat region; a trench is a long underwater mountain chain
options.D: A ridge is a shallow submerged extension of a continent; a trench is a deep-ocean-floor feature

questions.explanation: A ridge forms at a divergent boundary where new oceanic crust is created; a trench forms at a convergent boundary where oceanic lithosphere is subducted.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a mountain pass?

options.A: A relatively low route or gap across a mountain range, often used for transport and communication between valleys or regions
options.B: The highest peak of a mountain range
options.C: A deep valley cut by a river through a mountain range
options.D: A steep cliff face on a mountain

questions.explanation: A mountain pass is a relatively low route or gap across a mountain range, often used for transport and communication between valleys or regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How are mountain passes formed?

options.A: They may be produced by river erosion, glacial erosion, tectonic structure, faulting or differential weathering; some are saddles between peaks
options.B: They are formed only by volcanic eruptions
options.C: They are formed only by wind deposition
options.D: They are formed only by seafloor spreading

questions.explanation: Mountain passes may be produced by river erosion, glacial erosion, tectonic structure, faulting or differential weathering. Some are saddles between peaks.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are mountain passes important?

options.A: They provide routes for roads, railways, trade, migration and military movement through otherwise difficult mountainous terrain
options.B: They are the highest points of mountain ranges
options.C: They are the deepest valleys in mountain ranges
options.D: They are the steepest cliffs in mountain ranges

questions.explanation: Mountain passes provide routes for roads, railways, trade, migration and military movement through otherwise difficult mountainous terrain.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct major divisions of a simplified ocean-floor cross-section?

options.A: Continental shelf, continental slope, continental rise and deep-ocean basin
options.D: Continental crust, mantle, outer core and inner core

questions.explanation: The simplified ocean-floor cross-section consists of the continental shelf, continental slope, continental rise and deep-ocean basin. The deep-ocean basin includes abyssal plains, trenches and mid-oceanic ridges.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a continental margin?

options.A: The deepest portion of an ocean
options.B: The submerged outer edge of a continent extending towards the deep ocean floor
options.C: A chain of underwater volcanic mountains
options.D: A narrow depression formed by wind erosion

questions.explanation: A continental margin is the submerged outer edge of a continent. It includes the continental shelf, continental slope and, where developed, the continental rise.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic is generally associated with an active continental margin?

options.A: Broad continental shelf and absence of earthquakes
options.C: Earthquakes, volcanism and possible ocean trenches

questions.explanation: Active continental margins occur near active plate boundaries and commonly experience earthquakes, volcanism and trenches. They may also have narrow continental shelves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is generally characteristic of a passive continental margin?

options.A: Frequent volcanic activity and active subduction
options.B: Broad continental shelf and thick sediment accumulation
options.C: Permanent presence of deep ocean trenches
options.D: Continuous formation of volcanic island arcs

questions.explanation: Passive continental margins are generally farther from active plate boundaries and commonly possess broad shelves and thick sediment accumulations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a continental shelf?

options.A: A deep depression in the ocean floor
options.B: A gently sloping submerged extension of a continent
options.D: A volcanic island located in the ocean

questions.explanation: A continental shelf is a gently sloping submerged extension of a continent extending from the shoreline to the shelf break.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the shelf break?

options.A: The boundary between the continental shelf and the steeper continental slope
options.B: The boundary between the ocean and the atmosphere
options.C: The deepest portion of the continental rise
options.D: The point where an ocean trench begins

questions.explanation: The shelf break is the point or zone where the gently sloping continental shelf transitions into the steeper continental slope.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At approximately what depth is the continental shelf break commonly found?

options.A: 10–20 metres

questions.explanation: The continental shelf break commonly occurs at around 100–200 metres depth, although the actual depth varies considerably.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the commonly quoted global average width of a continental shelf?

options.A: 10–20 kilometres

questions.explanation: The commonly quoted global average width of continental shelves is approximately 70–80 kilometres. However, their actual width varies considerably.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important economic resource associated with continental shelves?

options.A: Offshore petroleum and natural gas

questions.explanation: Continental shelves support fisheries, offshore petroleum and natural-gas extraction, seabed minerals, marine transport and renewable-energy installations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are continental shelves often productive fishing grounds?

options.A: They have extremely high water pressure
options.B: Shallow water allows sunlight penetration, while nutrient inputs support plankton and marine food webs
options.D: They are permanently covered by glaciers

questions.explanation: Shallow shelf waters allow sunlight to support photosynthesis. Nutrients supplied through mixing, upwelling and river inputs sustain plankton and marine food webs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Along which part of India's continental margin is a relatively broad continental shelf found in several sectors?

options.A: Eastern Himalayan margin

questions.explanation: The western continental margin of India has a relatively broad continental shelf in several sectors, particularly off parts of Gujarat and the west coast.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a continental slope?

options.A: A shallow, flat coastal plain
options.B: A relatively steep submarine descent extending from the shelf break towards the deep ocean
options.C: A depositional plain formed by wind
options.D: A shallow lagoon separated by a sandbar

questions.explanation: The continental slope is the relatively steep submarine region extending from the shelf break towards the deep-ocean floor or continental rise.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature may deeply cut into a continental slope?

options.A: Sand dunes

questions.explanation: Continental slopes may be cut by deep submarine canyons, which are often associated with turbidity currents and submarine mass movements.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a turbidity current?

options.A: A warm surface current driven by sunlight
options.B: A dense sediment-laden current flowing downslope under gravity along the seabed
options.C: A current formed exclusively by melting polar ice
options.D: A wind current carrying desert sand

questions.explanation: A turbidity current is a dense, sediment-laden underwater current that flows downslope under gravity and can transport large quantities of sediment.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main role of submarine canyons in sediment transfer?

options.A: They transport sediments from the deep ocean to mountain peaks
options.B: They channel sediments from continental shelves and slopes towards deep-sea fans and ocean basins

questions.explanation: Submarine canyons provide pathways through which sediments are transported from continental shelves and slopes to deep-sea fans and deep-ocean basins.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a continental rise?

options.A: A steep volcanic mountain on the ocean floor
options.B: A broad, gently sloping accumulation of sediment at the base of a continental slope
options.D: A deep depression at a convergent plate boundary

questions.explanation: A continental rise is a broad, gently sloping sediment accumulation zone at the base of a continental slope.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which processes commonly contribute to the formation of a continental rise?

options.A: Wind erosion and volcanic explosions only
options.B: Turbidity currents, submarine landslides and other mass-flow processes

questions.explanation: Continental rises commonly form through the accumulation of sediments transported downslope by turbidity currents, submarine landslides and other mass-flow processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Along which type of continental margin is the continental rise generally best developed?

options.A: Active continental margins with deep trenches

questions.explanation: Continental rises are generally well developed along many passive continental margins. They may be narrow, poorly developed or absent along active margins where trenches occur.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a submarine fan?

options.A: A fan-shaped sediment accumulation at the foot of a submarine canyon or slope
options.C: A coral reef located in shallow water

questions.explanation: A submarine fan is a fan-shaped accumulation of sediment deposited by sediment-laden flows at the foot of a submarine canyon or slope. Large examples are called deep-sea fans.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an ocean basin?

options.A: A vast depression in the Earth's crust occupied by ocean water
options.C: A mountain range on a continent

questions.explanation: An ocean basin is a vast depression in the Earth's crust occupied by ocean water and underlain mainly by oceanic crust.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How many major ocean basins are identified in the PDF?

options.A: Three

questions.explanation: The five major ocean basins are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic ocean basins.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a major feature of ocean basins in the PDF?

options.A: Abyssal plains

questions.explanation: The listed ocean-basin features include abyssal plains, mid-ocean ridges, ocean trenches, seamounts, guyots, fracture zones, submarine plateaus and deep-sea fans.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination of processes creates and modifies ocean basins?

options.A: Plate tectonics, seafloor spreading, subduction, volcanism, faulting and sedimentation

questions.explanation: Ocean basins are created and reshaped by plate tectonics, seafloor spreading, subduction, volcanism, faulting, sedimentation and changes in sea level.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the principal composition of oceanic crust?

options.A: Granite and sandstone

questions.explanation: Oceanic crust is predominantly basaltic to gabbroic in composition. It is generally thinner and denser than continental crust.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an abyssal plain?

options.A: A broad, extremely flat or gently sloping region of the deep-ocean floor

questions.explanation: An abyssal plain is an extensive, extremely flat or gently sloping area of the deep-ocean floor.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At what approximate depth do abyssal plains commonly occur?

options.A: 100–500 metres

questions.explanation: Abyssal plains commonly occur at depths of approximately 3,000–6,000 metres.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How are abyssal plains mainly formed?

options.A: By accumulation of fine sediments that bury irregular oceanic crust and volcanic relief
options.B: By wind erosion of continental mountains
options.C: By the collapse of mountain peaks
options.D: By the formation of coral islands

questions.explanation: Fine sediments, including clay and remains of microscopic marine organisms, gradually accumulate and bury irregular oceanic crust and volcanic relief.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are abyssal plains among the flattest regions on Earth?

options.A: Continuous volcanic eruptions level the ocean floor
options.B: Long-term accumulation of fine-grained sediments fills depressions and smooths underlying relief
options.D: Tectonic plates stop moving in these regions

questions.explanation: Long-term accumulation of fine-grained sediments smooths the underlying ocean-floor relief and fills depressions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which set of conditions is characteristic of abyssal plains?

options.A: Shallow water, warm temperatures and low pressure
options.B: Great depth, darkness, cold water and high pressure
options.C: High sunlight and dense terrestrial vegetation
options.D: Strong winds and dry sandy surfaces

questions.explanation: Abyssal plains are characterised by great depth, very low gradient, extensive area, darkness, cold water and high pressure.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which oceans are abyssal plains particularly found according to the PDF?

options.A: Atlantic, Indian and Pacific

questions.explanation: Abyssal plains occur in the deep Atlantic, Indian and Pacific oceans, especially where sediment supply is sufficient to bury rough basement topography.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an ocean trench?

options.A: A broad, flat region of the deep-ocean floor
options.B: A long, narrow and extremely deep depression in the ocean floor

questions.explanation: An ocean trench is a long, narrow and very deep depression in the ocean floor, generally associated with convergent plate boundaries and subduction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Ocean trenches are generally formed at which type of plate boundary?

options.A: Divergent boundary

questions.explanation: Ocean trenches generally form at convergent plate boundaries where one tectonic plate subducts beneath another.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does an ocean trench form at a subduction zone?

options.A: An oceanic plate bends and descends into the mantle
options.B: Two plates move apart and create a rift valley
options.C: River sediments accumulate at a river mouth
options.D: Wind deposits sand along the coastline

questions.explanation: At a subduction zone, a dense oceanic lithospheric plate bends and descends into the mantle, producing a deep trench near the plate boundary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is the deepest known ocean trench?

options.A: Tonga Trench

questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific is the deepest known ocean trench.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the name of the deepest surveyed area of the Mariana Trench?

options.A: Challenger Deep

questions.explanation: Challenger Deep is the deepest surveyed area of the Mariana Trench. Its measured depth estimates are around 10.9 kilometres, with values varying according to survey and method.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following combinations contains only major ocean trenches listed in the PDF?

options.A: Tonga, Philippine, Japan and Kuril–Kamchatka
options.D: Zoji La, Nathu La, Shipki La and Banihal

questions.explanation: Other major ocean trenches listed in the PDF include Tonga, Philippine, Japan, Kuril–Kamchatka, Peru–Chile and Puerto Rico.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are ocean trenches commonly associated with earthquakes?

options.A: Because of strong evaporation
options.B: Because tectonic plates interact, lock, slip and deform at subduction zones

questions.explanation: Subduction zones generate earthquakes as tectonic plates interact, lock, slip and deform. Very large earthquakes can occur along the plate interface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a mid-oceanic ridge?

options.A: A long underwater mountain chain formed mainly at divergent plate boundaries
options.B: A narrow depression formed by subduction
options.C: A coastal sand ridge formed by waves

questions.explanation: Mid-oceanic ridges are long underwater mountain chains formed mainly at divergent plate boundaries where tectonic plates move apart and new oceanic crust is produced.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process is mainly responsible for the formation of new oceanic crust at mid-oceanic ridges?

options.A: Wind deposition
options.B: Rising mantle material, decompression melting and cooling of magma

questions.explanation: As plates diverge, mantle material rises and partially melts due to decompression. The magma cools and forms new oceanic crust.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is seafloor spreading?

options.A: The process by which new oceanic lithosphere forms at mid-ocean ridges and moves outward on both sides
options.B: The process of forming coastal sand dunes
options.C: The process of depositing river sediments
options.D: The process of forming continental mountains by erosion

questions.explanation: Seafloor spreading is the formation of new oceanic lithosphere at mid-ocean ridges and its outward movement on both sides as tectonic plates separate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following features may occur along mid-oceanic ridges?

options.A: Central rift valleys, hydrothermal vents, volcanism and shallow earthquakes

questions.explanation: Mid-oceanic ridges form a globally connected submarine mountain system. Slow-spreading sections commonly have central rift valleys and the ridges experience volcanic activity, shallow earthquakes and hydrothermal vent activity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the longest mountain chain on Earth?

options.A: Himalayas

questions.explanation: The global mid-ocean ridge system is the longest mountain chain on Earth, extending for tens of thousands of kilometres beneath the oceans.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is a major part of which geological system?

options.A: Global mid-ocean ridge system

questions.explanation: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is a major section of the global mid-ocean ridge system running through the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a mid-ocean ridge from an ocean trench?

options.A: Both form only at divergent boundaries
options.B: A ridge forms at a divergent boundary, while a trench forms at a convergent subduction boundary
options.C: A ridge forms through wind erosion, while a trench forms through river erosion
options.D: A trench produces new oceanic crust, while a ridge destroys it

questions.explanation: Mid-ocean ridges form where plates diverge and new oceanic crust is produced. Ocean trenches form where oceanic lithosphere is subducted at convergent boundaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a mountain pass?

options.A: A relatively low route or gap across a mountain range
options.B: The highest peak in a mountain range

questions.explanation: A mountain pass is a relatively low route or gap across a mountain range, often used for transport and communication between valleys or regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following processes can contribute to the formation of mountain passes?

options.A: River erosion, glacial erosion, tectonic structure, faulting and differential weathering

questions.explanation: Mountain passes may be produced by river erosion, glacial erosion, tectonic structures, faulting or differential weathering. Some are saddle-shaped depressions between peaks.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are mountain passes geographically and strategically important?

options.A: They provide routes for transport, trade, migration and military movement
options.C: They are used exclusively for mining
options.D: They are the main locations of oceanic crust formation

questions.explanation: Mountain passes provide routes for roads, railways, trade, migration and military movement through otherwise difficult mountainous terrain.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as an important mountain pass in India in the PDF?

options.A: Zoji La

questions.explanation: The listed Indian mountain passes include Zoji La, Banihal, Shipki La, Nathu La, Jelep La, Rohtang Pass, Baralacha La, Khardung La, Lipulekh and Bomdi La.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Nathu La is located in which Indian state?

options.A: Himachal Pradesh

questions.explanation: Nathu La is located in Sikkim on the India–China border and forms part of a historic trade route.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Zoji La connects which two regions?

options.A: Kashmir Valley and Ladakh

questions.explanation: Zoji La is located in the western Himalayas and connects the Kashmir Valley with the Ladakh region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Shipki La is located in which Indian state?

options.A: Sikkim

questions.explanation: Shipki La is located in Himachal Pradesh on the India–China border in the Sutlej valley region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a col in mountain geography?

options.A: A deep ocean basin
options.B: A low saddle-like depression between mountain peaks

questions.explanation: A col is a low saddle-like depression between mountain peaks and may sometimes form a mountain pass.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a waterfall?

options.A: A vertical or near-vertical descent of river water over a rock step or steep channel break
options.B: A slow-moving river on a flat plain

questions.explanation: A waterfall is a vertical or near-vertical descent of river water over a rock step or steep break in the river channel.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geological condition commonly contributes to waterfall formation through differential erosion?

options.A: Hard rock overlying softer rock
options.B: Uniformly soft sediment without any gradient

questions.explanation: Where hard rock overlies softer rock, the softer layer erodes more rapidly and the resistant layer forms a ledge, contributing to waterfall formation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified as a possible cause of waterfall formation in the PDF?

options.A: Faults and fractures

questions.explanation: Waterfalls may form due to resistant and softer rock layers, faults, fractures, plateau edges, glacial overdeepening and changes in river-channel level.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a plunge pool?

options.A: A shallow pool formed by rainfall on a plateau
options.B: A deep basin at the foot of a waterfall formed by falling water and rock abrasion
options.C: A pool located on a mountain summit

questions.explanation: A plunge pool is a deep basin at the foot of a waterfall formed by the impact of falling water and abrasion by transported rock fragments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is waterfall retreat?

options.A: The downstream movement of a waterfall
options.B: The upstream migration of a waterfall caused by erosion and collapse of rock
options.C: The complete drying of a river
options.D: The formation of a river delta

questions.explanation: Waterfall retreat is the upstream migration of a waterfall as erosion undercuts its base and causes blocks of rock to collapse.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Jog Falls is located on which river?

options.A: Kaveri

questions.explanation: Jog Falls is located on the Sharavathi River in Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Dudhsagar Falls is associated with which river system?

options.A: Mandovi

questions.explanation: Dudhsagar Falls, in the Goa–Karnataka region, is located in the Mandovi River system in the Western Ghats.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only waterfalls listed in the PDF?

options.A: Jog, Kunchikal, Dudhsagar and Athirappilly
options.D: Kunchikal, Grand Canyon, Athirappilly and Nathu La

questions.explanation: The waterfalls listed in the PDF are Jog Falls, Kunchikal Falls, Dudhsagar Falls, Athirappilly Falls, Nohkalikai Falls and Hogenakkal Falls.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a waterfall from rapids?

options.A: A waterfall has a marked steep or near-vertical drop, whereas rapids are turbulent stretches of fast-flowing water
options.B: Rapids always have a vertical drop greater than waterfalls
options.D: There is no difference between waterfalls and rapids

questions.explanation: A waterfall has a marked steep or near-vertical drop. Rapids are turbulent stretches where water flows rapidly over an irregular or steep channel without one dominant vertical fall.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a canyon?

options.A: A deep valley with steep sides, commonly formed by prolonged river incision

questions.explanation: A canyon is a deep valley with steep sides, commonly formed by prolonged river incision into bedrock, often in uplifted or arid regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which factors can help maintain the steep walls of a canyon?

options.A: Tectonic uplift, resistant rock layers and limited lateral erosion

questions.explanation: Canyons develop through prolonged river downcutting. Tectonic uplift, resistant rock layers and limited lateral erosion can help maintain their steep walls.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Grand Canyon is located in which US state?

options.A: California

questions.explanation: The Grand Canyon is located in Arizona, United States, and was carved by the Colorado River.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river carved the Grand Canyon?

options.A: Mississippi River

questions.explanation: The Colorado River has cut deeply into the Colorado Plateau, creating the Grand Canyon and exposing a sequence of rock layers that records geological history.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a gorge?

options.A: A narrow, deep valley with steep or nearly vertical sides

questions.explanation: A gorge is a narrow, deep valley with steep or nearly vertical sides, commonly formed by river erosion and downcutting.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which conditions commonly encourage the formation of a gorge?

options.A: River downcutting, tectonic uplift, resistant bedrock or a steep gradient

questions.explanation: A gorge forms as a river cuts vertically into rock, particularly where uplift, resistant bedrock or a steep gradient encourages downcutting.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a well-known gorge mentioned in the PDF?

options.A: Kali Gandaki Gorge

questions.explanation: The Kali Gandaki Gorge in Nepal and river gorges in the Himalayas are examples mentioned in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement best explains the commonly used distinction between a canyon and a gorge?

options.A: A canyon is often larger and broader, whereas a gorge is often narrower and tighter
options.B: A canyon is always underwater, whereas a gorge is always on land
options.C: A gorge is formed by wind, whereas a canyon is formed by tides
options.D: They are completely unrelated geographical features

questions.explanation: Both are deep valleys with steep sides. Canyon commonly refers to a very large or extensive valley, while gorge often refers to a narrower valley. There is no strict universal boundary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a delta?

options.A: A depositional landform formed when a river deposits sediment near its mouth
options.B: A deep ocean depression formed by subduction
options.C: A mountain pass formed by glacial erosion

questions.explanation: A delta is a depositional landform formed when a river enters a standing body of water, loses transport capacity and deposits sediment near its mouth.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What happens to a river's velocity and sediment-carrying capacity when it enters a standing body of water?

options.A: Both generally increase
options.B: Both generally decrease, encouraging sediment deposition
options.C: Velocity increases while carrying capacity becomes unlimited

questions.explanation: When a river enters slower-moving water, its velocity and carrying capacity decrease. Sand, silt and clay are deposited, helping form a delta.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination of conditions generally favours delta formation?

options.A: Large sediment supply, shallow receiving basin, low wave and tidal energy and sufficient accommodation space
options.B: No sediment supply and extremely strong wave action
options.C: Very deep receiving basin and no deposition

questions.explanation: Large sediment supply, a relatively shallow receiving basin, low wave and tidal energy and sufficient accommodation space favour delta growth. Strong waves and tides can reshape or limit deltas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are distributaries?

options.A: Channels that branch away from the main river near its mouth
options.D: Ocean currents flowing parallel to the coast

questions.explanation: Distributaries are channels that branch away from the main river near its mouth and distribute water and sediment across a delta.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a commonly recognised descriptive type of delta?

options.A: Arcuate delta

questions.explanation: Common descriptive types of deltas include arcuate, bird's-foot, cuspate and tide-dominated or estuarine forms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a classic example of an arcuate delta?

options.A: Nile Delta

questions.explanation: The Nile Delta is a classic example of an arcuate delta, which has a roughly triangular or fan-shaped form with a curved seaward margin.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which delta is a classic example of a bird's-foot delta?

options.A: Nile Delta

questions.explanation: The Mississippi Delta is a classic bird's-foot delta, characterised by long distributary channels extending seaward like toes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which delta is often cited as an example of a cuspate delta?

options.A: Tiber Delta

questions.explanation: The Tiber Delta is often cited as a cuspate delta. It has a pointed or tooth-shaped form produced where river sediment is reworked by waves from both sides.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following contains only important Indian deltas listed in the PDF?

options.A: Ganga–Brahmaputra, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri
options.B: Narmada, Tapi, Mandovi, Zuari and Hooghly

questions.explanation: Important Indian deltas listed in the PDF are the Ganga–Brahmaputra Delta, Mahanadi Delta, Godavari Delta, Krishna Delta and Kaveri Delta.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the world's largest delta system according to the PDF?

options.A: Nile Delta

questions.explanation: The Ganga–Brahmaputra–Meghna delta system, shared by Bangladesh and India, is the world's largest delta system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are deltas important for agriculture?

options.A: They commonly contain fertile alluvial soils and abundant water
options.B: They contain only barren rocky surfaces
options.D: They are permanently covered by glaciers

questions.explanation: Deltas commonly contain deep, fertile alluvial soils and abundant water, supporting intensive agriculture and dense settlement. However, they are vulnerable to floods and salinity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an estuary?

options.A: A partly enclosed coastal water body where freshwater mixes with seawater
options.B: A mountain valley formed by glaciers
options.D: A river-mouth depositional landform made entirely of sand

questions.explanation: An estuary is a partly enclosed coastal water body where freshwater from rivers mixes with seawater, creating brackish water and strong tidal influence.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process commonly contributes to the formation of an estuary?

options.A: Flooding of a river valley due to rising sea level
options.D: Deposition of loess on a plateau

questions.explanation: Estuaries commonly form where a river valley is flooded by rising sea level or where coastal processes create a partly enclosed inlet through which freshwater and seawater mix.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is brackish water?

options.A: Water with salinity between freshwater and seawater

questions.explanation: Brackish water has salinity between that of freshwater and seawater and is commonly found in estuaries and lagoons.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of estuaries?

options.A: Variable salinity and strong tidal influence
options.D: Only freshwater conditions throughout the year

questions.explanation: Estuaries are influenced by tides, receive freshwater and marine water, have variable salinity, trap or transport sediments and support productive ecosystems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important ecological function of estuaries?

options.A: Providing nursery habitats for fish and crustaceans

questions.explanation: Estuaries provide nursery habitats for fish and crustaceans, feeding grounds for birds, nutrient cycling, sediment trapping and coastal protection.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following rivers is listed as an example of an estuarine system in India?

options.A: Narmada

questions.explanation: Indian estuarine examples listed in the PDF include the Narmada, Tapi, Mandovi, Zuari and Hooghly.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are estuaries common along parts of India's western coast?

options.A: The western coastal plain is relatively narrow, rivers are often short and swift, and river mouths experience tidal influence
options.B: The western coastal plain is extremely broad and has no rivers
options.C: The region has no interaction with seawater

questions.explanation: The western coastal plain is relatively narrow, rivers are often short and swift, and many river mouths are influenced by tides, favouring estuarine conditions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a delta from an estuary?

options.A: A delta is mainly depositional and commonly has distributaries, while an estuary is a tidal mixing zone of freshwater and seawater
options.B: A delta is formed by wind, while an estuary is formed by glaciers
options.D: An estuary is always freshwater, while a delta is always saline

questions.explanation: A delta is built mainly through sediment deposition at a river mouth and commonly has distributaries. An estuary is a tidal river mouth or coastal inlet where freshwater and seawater mix. Some river mouths show features of both.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a lagoon?

options.A: A shallow coastal water body partly or almost completely separated from the open sea by a barrier
options.D: A river channel located far inland

questions.explanation: A lagoon is a shallow coastal water body separated from the open sea partly or almost completely by a sandbar, barrier island, reef or spit.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which coastal processes commonly contribute to lagoon formation?

options.A: Wave action and longshore currents building bars or spits

questions.explanation: Waves and longshore currents can build bars or spits across coastal indentations, enclosing shallow water. Coral reefs can also enclose lagoons.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about lagoon water is correct?

options.A: It is always freshwater
options.C: It may be freshwater, brackish or saline depending on inflows and connections
options.D: It always has the same salinity as the open ocean

questions.explanation: Lagoons are generally shallow and may contain freshwater, brackish water or saline water depending on their inflows and connections with the sea.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following contains only important Indian lagoons listed in the PDF?

options.A: Chilika, Pulicat and Vembanad

questions.explanation: The important Indian lagoons listed are Chilika Lake in Odisha, Pulicat Lake on the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu coast and Vembanad Lake in Kerala.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Chilika Lake is located in which Indian state?

options.A: Kerala

questions.explanation: Chilika Lake is a large brackish-water coastal lagoon in Odisha.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geographical feature separates Chilika Lake from the Bay of Bengal?

options.A: A barrier spit

questions.explanation: Chilika Lake is separated from the Bay of Bengal by a barrier spit and connected to the sea through an inlet.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a lagoon from an estuary?

options.A: A lagoon is separated from the open sea by a barrier or reef, whereas an estuary is a tidal river mouth where freshwater and seawater mix
options.B: A lagoon is always deep, whereas an estuary is always dry
options.C: Both are formed exclusively by subduction
options.D: An estuary is a wind-deposited landform

questions.explanation: A lagoon is partly separated from the open sea by a barrier or reef. An estuary is a tidal river mouth where freshwater and seawater mix. Both can contain brackish water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a sand dune?

options.A: A hill or mound of loose sand formed by wind deposition
options.B: A deep depression formed by tectonic movement
options.D: A sediment deposit formed exclusively by rivers

questions.explanation: A sand dune is a hill or mound of loose sand formed by wind deposition, commonly found in deserts and coastal regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination of processes transports sand under wind action?

options.A: Saltation, surface creep and suspension

questions.explanation: Wind transports sand through saltation, surface creep and suspension. When wind speed decreases or an obstacle traps sand, particles accumulate and a dune grows.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is saltation in the context of sand transportation?

options.A: The bouncing or hopping movement of sand-sized particles along the ground
options.B: The rolling of large rocks down a mountain
options.C: The dissolution of minerals in seawater
options.D: The movement of sediments through underground rivers

questions.explanation: Saltation is the bouncing or hopping movement of sand-sized particles along the ground under wind action.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is surface creep?

options.A: The rolling or sliding of larger sand grains along the ground
options.B: The upward movement of water through rocks
options.C: The suspension of clay in deep ocean water
options.D: The formation of a river waterfall

questions.explanation: Surface creep is the rolling or sliding movement of larger sand grains along the ground, often pushed by impacts from saltating grains.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly identifies the main parts of a typical sand dune?

options.A: Windward slope, crest and leeward slip face

questions.explanation: A typical dune has a windward slope, a crest and a steeper leeward slip face.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the angle of repose?

options.A: The steepest stable angle at which loose granular material can rest without sliding
options.B: The angle between two tectonic plates
options.C: The angle of a river entering the sea
options.D: The angle of inclination of a continental shelf

questions.explanation: The angle of repose is the steepest stable angle at which loose granular material can rest without sliding.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the commonly quoted angle of repose for dry sand?

options.A: 5–10 degrees

questions.explanation: The angle of repose for dry sand is commonly around 30–35 degrees, depending on grain properties and moisture.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major type of sand dune listed in the PDF?

options.A: Barchan

questions.explanation: The major dune types listed are barchan, transverse, longitudinal, parabolic and star dunes. Arcuate is a type of delta.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of sand dune is crescent-shaped and commonly forms where sand supply is limited?

options.A: Star dune

questions.explanation: A barchan dune is crescent-shaped and forms where sand supply is limited and wind direction is mainly one-way.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which direction do the horns of a barchan dune point?

options.A: Upwind

questions.explanation: The horns of a barchan dune point downwind, an important distinction for examination questions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A transverse dune is generally oriented in which direction relative to the prevailing wind?

options.A: Parallel to the prevailing wind
options.C: At exactly 45 degrees to the wind
options.D: Without any relation to wind direction

questions.explanation: Transverse dunes are ridges oriented broadly perpendicular to the prevailing wind, usually where sand supply is abundant and wind direction is relatively consistent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of dune is a long, narrow ridge aligned broadly parallel to the resultant wind direction?

options.A: Barchan

questions.explanation: Longitudinal dunes, also called linear or seif dunes, are long, narrow ridges aligned broadly parallel to the resultant wind direction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of sand dune is U-shaped and commonly has arms pointing upwind?

options.A: Barchan

questions.explanation: A parabolic dune is U-shaped, and its arms generally point upwind. The arms are often anchored by vegetation, and these dunes are common in coastal settings.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of sand dune is characterised by multiple arms and commonly forms under variable wind directions?

options.A: Star dune

questions.explanation: Star dunes have multiple arms and form under variable wind directions, commonly where sand supplies are large.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Indian region contains extensive sand dunes?

options.A: Thar Desert of Rajasthan

questions.explanation: The Thar Desert of Rajasthan contains extensive sand dunes. Coastal dunes also occur along parts of India's coastline.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main difference between active and stabilised sand dunes?

options.A: Active dunes are mobile under wind action, while stabilised dunes are held in place by vegetation, moisture, crusts or human intervention
options.B: Active dunes contain no sand, while stabilised dunes contain only rock
options.D: Stabilised dunes move faster than active dunes

questions.explanation: Active dunes are mobile under wind action. Stabilised dunes are held in place partly by vegetation, moisture, crusts or human intervention.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is loess?

options.A: A widespread deposit of wind-blown silt

questions.explanation: Loess is a widespread, usually unstratified deposit of wind-blown silt, commonly pale yellow or buff in colour.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which particle size is dominant in loess deposits?

options.A: Gravel-sized particles

questions.explanation: Loess contains a high proportion of silt-sized particles and is commonly a fine-grained, wind-blown deposit.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following can provide the fine sediment from which loess deposits develop?

options.A: Glacial grinding, desert weathering and floodplain drying

questions.explanation: Fine sediment may be produced by glacial grinding, desert weathering, floodplain drying or other processes before being transported by wind and deposited over broad areas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of loess deposits?

options.A: Porous, fine-grained and commonly weakly stratified or unstratified
options.C: Permanently submerged under deep ocean water

questions.explanation: Loess is commonly porous, fine-grained and weakly stratified or unstratified. It may form steep-sided vertical bluffs and can be susceptible to erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why can loess soils be agriculturally fertile?

options.A: They commonly contain abundant silt and mineral nutrients and can retain moisture
options.C: They are made entirely of impermeable rock
options.D: They have no capacity to retain moisture

questions.explanation: Loess soils commonly contain abundant silt and mineral nutrients and can retain moisture. Their actual fertility depends on climate, soil development and land management.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which region is the best-known large area of loess deposits?

options.A: Loess Plateau of northern China

questions.explanation: The Loess Plateau of northern China is the best-known large region of loess deposits. Extensive deposits also occur in parts of Europe, Central Asia, North America and Argentina.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which description correctly identifies the Loess Plateau?

options.A: A large region of thick wind-blown silt deposits in north-central China
options.B: A deep marine basin in the Atlantic Ocean
options.C: A coastal lagoon in southern India
options.D: A volcanic island chain in the Pacific Ocean

questions.explanation: The Loess Plateau is a large region of thick wind-blown silt deposits in north-central China. It is deeply dissected by gullies and has historically experienced severe soil erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes loess from sand dunes?
