options.A: Loess consists mainly of wind-deposited silt, whereas dunes are mainly formed from wind-deposited sand
options.B: Loess is made of gravel, whereas dunes are made of clay
options.C: Loess forms only underwater, whereas dunes form only in mountains
options.D: Both consist entirely of volcanic rocks

questions.explanation: Loess consists mainly of wind-deposited silt spread in blankets, whereas sand dunes are mounds or ridges formed mainly from wind-deposited sand.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two marine regions are associated with the continental margins around the Indian subcontinent?

options.A: Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal
options.D: Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico

questions.explanation: The Indian continental margins are associated with the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group contains the mountain passes highlighted for quick revision in the PDF?

options.A: Zoji La, Nathu La, Shipki La, Rohtang Pass, Banihal and Lipulekh
options.B: Khardung La, Mariana Deep, Zoji La, Nile Pass and Nathu La
options.C: Nathu La, Chilika, Pulicat, Banihal and Vembanad
options.D: Rohtang Pass, Grand Canyon, Shipki La and Kaveri

questions.explanation: The quick-revision list highlights Zoji La, Nathu La, Shipki La, Rohtang Pass, Banihal and Lipulekh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches an Indian waterfall with its river?

options.A: Jog Falls – Sharavathi River

questions.explanation: Jog Falls is located on the Sharavathi River in Karnataka. Dudhsagar Falls is associated with the Mandovi River system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination contains only Indian deltas listed in the PDF?

options.A: Ganga–Brahmaputra, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri
options.B: Narmada, Tapi, Mandovi, Zuari and Hooghly
options.C: Chilika, Pulicat, Vembanad and Loess Plateau

questions.explanation: The PDF lists the Ganga–Brahmaputra, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri deltas as important Indian examples.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following contains only Indian estuarine examples listed in the PDF?

options.A: Narmada, Tapi, Mandovi and Zuari

questions.explanation: The quick-revision list identifies Narmada, Tapi, Mandovi and Zuari as important Indian estuarine examples.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which set contains the three Indian lagoons highlighted in the PDF?

options.A: Chilika, Pulicat and Vembanad

questions.explanation: Chilika, Pulicat and Vembanad are the important Indian lagoons highlighted in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about loess deposits in India is consistent with the PDF?

options.A: The Thar Desert is identified as the world's largest loess region
options.B: No major Indian loess region is commonly emphasised in standard school geography
options.C: Chilika Lake is a major loess deposit
options.D: The Western Ghats are identified as the classic Loess Plateau

questions.explanation: The PDF notes that no major Indian loess region is commonly emphasised in standard school geography and identifies northern China as the classic world example.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which ocean-floor feature marks the end of the continental shelf?

options.A: Shelf break

questions.explanation: The continental shelf ends at the shelf break, where the seabed begins its steeper descent into the continental slope.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the continental shelf and continental slope?

options.A: The shelf is shallow and gently sloping, while the slope is comparatively steep
options.B: The shelf is deeper and steeper than the slope
options.D: The slope is a wind-deposited landform

questions.explanation: The continental shelf is a shallow, gently inclined submerged extension of the continent, whereas the continental slope is the steeper descent beyond the shelf break.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature is a sediment-built zone at the base of many continental slopes?

options.A: Continental rise

questions.explanation: The continental rise is a gentle sediment-built zone at the foot of many continental slopes. It may be absent near trenches.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which comparison between an abyssal plain and an ocean trench is correct?

options.A: An abyssal plain is broad and relatively flat, while a trench is narrow and extremely deep
options.B: An abyssal plain is always deeper and narrower than a trench
options.C: Both are formed only by wind deposition
options.D: A trench is a shallow extension of a continent

questions.explanation: Abyssal plains are broad, relatively flat deep-ocean regions, whereas trenches are narrow, elongated and extremely deep depressions associated with subduction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At which type of plate boundary is new oceanic crust generally created?

options.A: Convergent boundary

questions.explanation: New oceanic crust is created at divergent plate boundaries, particularly along mid-ocean ridges.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature is primarily associated with oceanic lithosphere being subducted?

options.A: Mid-ocean ridge

questions.explanation: Ocean trenches occur at convergent subduction boundaries where oceanic lithosphere bends and descends into the mantle.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about the Mariana Trench is correct?

options.A: Challenger Deep is its deepest surveyed area
options.B: It is located in the Atlantic Ocean

questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench is the deepest known ocean trench, and Challenger Deep is its deepest surveyed area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about mountain passes is correct?

options.A: They are low routes or gaps through mountain ranges
options.B: They are always the highest peaks in mountain ranges
options.D: They are depositional features at river mouths

questions.explanation: Mountain passes are relatively low routes or gaps through mountain ranges and should not be confused with mountain peaks.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a recognised mechanism of waterfall formation in the PDF?

options.A: Differential erosion

questions.explanation: Waterfalls may form through differential erosion, faulting, glaciation, plateau edges and changes in river-channel level. Loess deposition is a wind-related process.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about delta formation is correct?

options.A: It requires sediment deposition near a river mouth
options.B: It occurs only through tectonic subduction
options.C: It requires complete absence of sediment
options.D: It is exclusively a wind-depositional feature

questions.explanation: Delta formation requires sediment deposition at a river mouth. Strong waves and tides may reshape or inhibit delta growth.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature is characterised by tidal mixing of freshwater and seawater?

options.A: Estuary

questions.explanation: Estuaries are tidal mixing zones where freshwater and seawater meet, producing brackish water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which coastal feature is partly separated from the sea by a barrier or reef?

options.A: Lagoon

questions.explanation: A lagoon is a shallow coastal water body partly or almost completely separated from the open sea by a sandbar, barrier island, reef or spit.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly identifies the direction of the horns of barchan dunes and the arms of parabolic dunes?

options.A: Both point downwind
options.B: Barchan horns point downwind, while parabolic dune arms generally point upwind
options.C: Barchan horns point upwind, while parabolic arms point downwind

questions.explanation: Barchan horns point downwind, whereas the arms of parabolic dunes generally point upwind. This is an important examination distinction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a canyon from a gorge?

options.A: A canyon is often larger and broader, while a gorge is often narrower and tighter, although usage varies
options.B: A canyon is always formed by wind, while a gorge is always formed by tides
options.D: There is a universally fixed scientific boundary between the two terms

questions.explanation: Both are deep valleys with steep sides. Canyon often refers to a larger, broader valley, whereas gorge often refers to a narrower valley. There is no strict universal boundary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares loess and sand dunes?

options.A: Loess is mainly wind-blown silt, whereas dunes are mainly wind-deposited sand
options.B: Loess is a marine trench, whereas dunes are river valleys
options.C: Both are composed entirely of large rocks

questions.explanation: Loess is a wind-blown silt deposit, while sand dunes are mounds or ridges formed mainly by wind-deposited sand.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following statements about continental margins: 1. A continental shelf is part of the submerged continent. 2. A continental slope is steeper than a continental shelf. 3. A continental rise is generally formed by sediment accumulation. Which statements are correct?

options.A: 1 only

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. The shelf is a submerged continental extension, the slope is steeper, and the continental rise is a sediment accumulation zone at the foot of many continental slopes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Abyssal plains are broad and relatively flat. 2. Ocean trenches are narrow and extremely deep. 3. Both are primarily associated with wind deposition. Which statements are correct?

options.A: 1 only

questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Abyssal plains are broad and flat, while trenches are narrow and very deep. They are ocean-floor features, not primarily wind-depositional landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following statements about mid-ocean ridges: 1. They are mainly associated with divergent plate boundaries. 2. New oceanic crust forms there. 3. They are associated with shallow earthquakes and volcanic activity. Which statements are correct?

options.A: 1 only

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. Mid-ocean ridges form at divergent boundaries, produce new oceanic crust and commonly experience volcanic activity and shallow earthquakes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the general movement from the continental shelf towards the deep ocean floor?

options.A: Continental shelf → continental slope → continental rise → deep-ocean basin
options.B: Continental slope → continental shelf → ocean trench → continental rise
options.C: Deep-ocean basin → continental rise → continental shelf → continental slope
options.D: Continental rise → ocean trench → continental shelf → continental slope

questions.explanation: The general simplified sequence is continental shelf, continental slope, continental rise and deep-ocean basin. The rise may be absent or poorly developed along active margins with trenches.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched?

options.A: Mid-ocean ridge – Convergent boundary

questions.explanation: Mid-ocean ridges form at divergent boundaries where plates move apart and new oceanic crust is produced. Trenches are associated with convergent subduction boundaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination is correctly matched?

options.A: Jog Falls – Sharavathi River; Grand Canyon – Colorado River
options.B: Jog Falls – Narmada River; Grand Canyon – Nile River
options.C: Dudhsagar – Kaveri River; Grand Canyon – Amazon River
options.D: Kunchikal – Ganga River; Grand Canyon – Mississippi River

questions.explanation: Jog Falls is located on the Sharavathi River in Karnataka, while the Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon in Arizona.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination is correctly matched?

options.A: Nile – Arcuate delta; Mississippi – Bird's-foot delta; Tiber – Cuspate delta
options.B: Nile – Bird's-foot delta; Mississippi – Cuspate delta; Tiber – Arcuate delta
options.C: Nile – Cuspate delta; Mississippi – Arcuate delta; Tiber – Bird's-foot delta
options.D: All three are examples of estuaries

questions.explanation: The Nile Delta is a classic arcuate delta, the Mississippi Delta is a classic bird's-foot delta and the Tiber Delta is often cited as a cuspate delta.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the geographical feature with its defining characteristic?

options.A: Estuary – Tidal mixing of freshwater and seawater
options.B: Lagoon – Deep depression caused by subduction

questions.explanation: Estuaries are tidal mixing zones where freshwater and seawater meet. A lagoon is separated partly from the sea by a barrier, loess is wind-blown silt and a barchan is a crescent-shaped sand dune.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches all three dune characteristics?

options.A: Barchan – Crescent-shaped; Transverse – Perpendicular to prevailing wind; Parabolic – U-shaped with arms generally pointing upwind
options.B: Barchan – U-shaped; Transverse – Parallel to wind; Parabolic – Crescent-shaped
options.C: Barchan – Multi-armed; Transverse – Parallel to wind; Parabolic – Pointed delta
options.D: Barchan – Silt blanket; Transverse – Ocean ridge; Parabolic – Mountain pass

questions.explanation: Barchan dunes are crescent-shaped, transverse dunes are broadly perpendicular to prevailing wind and parabolic dunes are U-shaped with arms generally pointing upwind.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the location of an active continental margin?

options.A: It is generally located far from active plate boundaries
options.B: It lies near an active plate boundary
options.C: It is always located in the centre of an ocean basin
options.D: It is found exclusively along passive continental interiors

questions.explanation: An active continental margin lies near an active plate boundary and commonly experiences earthquakes, volcanism and tectonic deformation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination is most characteristic of a passive continental margin?

options.A: Broad shelf and thick sediment accumulation
options.D: Frequent large earthquakes along an active plate boundary

questions.explanation: Passive continental margins are generally farther from active plate boundaries and commonly have broad continental shelves and thick sediment accumulations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding active and passive continental margins: 1. Active margins commonly occur near plate boundaries. 2. Passive margins are generally farther from active plate boundaries. 3. Broad shelves and thick sediment deposits are commonly associated with passive margins. Which statements are correct?

options.A: 1 only

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. Active margins are associated with tectonic activity, whereas passive margins commonly possess broad shelves and thick sediment accumulations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following features may be associated with an active continental margin?

options.A: Earthquakes, volcanism and ocean trenches
options.B: Only broad shelves and thick sediments

questions.explanation: Active continental margins are associated with tectonic plate boundaries and commonly experience earthquakes, volcanism and trenches.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about the width of continental shelves is scientifically appropriate?

options.A: All continental shelves have an identical width
options.B: Continental shelves are always less than 10 kilometres wide
options.C: Their widths vary from very narrow to hundreds of kilometres
options.D: Every continental shelf is exactly 70 kilometres wide

questions.explanation: Continental shelf width varies considerably. Shelves range from very narrow to hundreds of kilometres wide, with a commonly quoted global average of approximately 70–80 kilometres.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which depth range is commonly associated with the continental shelf break?

options.A: 10–30 metres

questions.explanation: The continental shelf break commonly occurs at approximately 100–200 metres depth, although the depth varies considerably from one location to another.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Indian coastal region is specifically identified as having a relatively broad continental shelf in several sectors?

options.A: Western continental margin

questions.explanation: The western continental margin of India has a relatively broad shelf in several sectors, particularly off parts of Gujarat and the west coast.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as an economic importance of continental shelves?

options.A: Offshore petroleum extraction

questions.explanation: Continental shelves support fisheries, offshore petroleum and natural-gas extraction, marine transport, seabed minerals, renewable-energy installations and coastal ecosystems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following factors contributing to the productivity of continental shelf fisheries: 1. Sunlight penetration in shallow water. 2. Nutrient supply through mixing. 3. Upwelling and river inputs. Which statements are correct?

options.A: 1 only

questions.explanation: Shallow shelf waters allow sunlight to support photosynthesis, while mixing, upwelling and river inputs provide nutrients that sustain plankton and marine food webs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the commonly described gradient of a continental slope?

options.A: Always perfectly horizontal
options.B: Commonly a few degrees, although local slopes can be much steeper

questions.explanation: The gradient of a continental slope varies widely but commonly lies within a range of a few degrees. Local sections can be much steeper.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geological transition is commonly associated with the continental slope?

options.A: Transition from continental crust to oceanic crust
options.B: Transition from the inner core to the outer core
options.C: Transition from the atmosphere to the stratosphere
options.D: Transition from a river delta to a floodplain

questions.explanation: The continental slope commonly marks the transition from continental crust to oceanic crust, in addition to forming the steep descent from the shelf towards the deep ocean.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of underwater valley is associated with continental shelves and slopes?

options.A: Submarine canyon

questions.explanation: Submarine canyons are deep, steep-sided valleys cut into continental shelves and slopes. They are often associated with turbidity currents and submarine mass movements.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the transport of sediments through a submarine canyon?

options.A: Continental shelf or slope → submarine canyon → deep-sea fan → deep-ocean basin
options.B: Ocean trench → mountain pass → river delta → continental shelf
options.C: Abyssal plain → mountain peak → continental shelf → river mouth
options.D: Loess plateau → lagoon → ocean ridge → continental slope

questions.explanation: Submarine canyons can channel sediments from continental shelves and slopes towards deep-sea fans and the deep-ocean basin.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following processes contributes to the development of continental rises?

options.A: Turbidity currents, submarine landslides and other mass-flow processes

questions.explanation: Continental rises commonly develop through the accumulation of sediments transported downslope by turbidity currents, submarine landslides and other mass-flow processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What happens to the continental rise along some active continental margins?

options.A: It is always extremely broad
options.B: It may be narrow, poorly developed or absent where trenches occur
options.D: It is replaced by a river delta in every case

questions.explanation: Continental rises are generally well developed along many passive continental margins but may be narrow, poorly developed or absent along active margins where trenches occur.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which term is used for large submarine fans?

options.A: Deep-sea fans

questions.explanation: A submarine fan is a fan-shaped sediment accumulation at the foot of a submarine canyon or slope. Large examples are called deep-sea fans.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists the five major ocean basins?

options.A: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic
options.B: Pacific, Mediterranean, Red, Arabian and Baltic
options.C: Atlantic, Caribbean, Black, Caspian and Red
options.D: Indian, Arabian, Mediterranean, Baltic and Southern

questions.explanation: The five major ocean basins are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic ocean basins.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following processes can modify ocean basins?

options.A: Plate tectonics, sedimentation and changes in sea level

questions.explanation: Ocean basins are created and reshaped by plate tectonics, seafloor spreading, subduction, volcanism, faulting, sedimentation and changes in sea level.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares oceanic crust with continental crust?

options.A: Oceanic crust is generally thinner and denser
options.B: Oceanic crust is always thicker and less dense
options.C: Both have identical thickness and density
options.D: Oceanic crust consists entirely of sediment

questions.explanation: Oceanic crust is predominantly basaltic to gabbroic in composition and is generally thinner and denser than continental crust.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Mariana Trench is situated in which ocean?

options.A: Atlantic Ocean

questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench is located in the western Pacific Ocean and is the deepest known ocean trench.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the approximate measured depth of Challenger Deep stated in the PDF?

options.A: Approximately 1.9 kilometres

questions.explanation: The PDF gives measured depth estimates around 10.9 kilometres for Challenger Deep. Actual estimates vary according to survey and measurement method.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following contains only ocean trenches mentioned in the PDF?

options.A: Tonga, Philippine, Japan and Puerto Rico
options.C: Kuril–Kamchatka, Zoji La, Japan and Tonga

questions.explanation: Tonga, Philippine, Japan, Kuril–Kamchatka, Peru–Chile and Puerto Rico are listed as other major ocean trenches.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which tectonic process explains the association between ocean trenches and volcanic arcs?

options.A: Subduction

questions.explanation: Ocean trenches occur at subduction zones, where oceanic lithosphere descends into the mantle. These zones are commonly associated with earthquakes and volcanic arcs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statements about earthquakes near ocean trenches are correct? 1. They are associated with subduction zones. 2. Tectonic plates may lock and subsequently slip. 3. Very large earthquakes can occur along the plate interface.

options.A: 1 only

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. Interactions, locking, slipping and deformation of plates at subduction zones generate earthquakes, including very large events.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What causes mantle material to partially melt beneath a mid-ocean ridge?

options.A: Decompression as mantle material rises

questions.explanation: At divergent boundaries, mantle material rises and partially melts because of decompression. The resulting magma cools to form new oceanic crust.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process describes the outward movement of newly formed oceanic lithosphere on both sides of a mid-ocean ridge?

options.A: Seafloor spreading

questions.explanation: Seafloor spreading is the process by which new oceanic lithosphere forms at mid-ocean ridges and moves outward on both sides as tectonic plates separate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A central rift valley is particularly associated with which sections of mid-ocean ridges?

options.A: Slow-spreading sections

questions.explanation: Mid-ocean ridges commonly have a central rift valley in slow-spreading sections. They also experience volcanic activity and shallow earthquakes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Hydrothermal vents are associated with which major ocean-floor feature?

options.A: Mid-oceanic ridges

questions.explanation: Mid-ocean ridges are sites of hydrothermal vents, along with volcanic activity and shallow earthquakes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which plates are separated by different segments of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge according to the PDF?

options.A: American plates and Eurasian and African plates

questions.explanation: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge runs through the Atlantic Ocean and separates the American plates from the Eurasian and African plates in different segments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a recognised function of mountain passes?

options.A: Providing transport and communication routes between mountainous regions

questions.explanation: Mountain passes provide routes for roads, railways, trade, migration and military movement through otherwise difficult mountainous terrain.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following processes can contribute to the formation of mountain passes? 1. River erosion. 2. Glacial erosion. 3. Faulting and differential weathering.

options.A: 1 only

questions.explanation: Mountain passes may form through river erosion, glacial erosion, tectonic structures, faulting and differential weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mountain pass is located on a historic India–China trade route in Sikkim?

options.A: Nathu La

questions.explanation: Nathu La is located in Sikkim on the India–China border and forms part of a historic trade route.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mountain pass connects the Kashmir Valley with the Ladakh region?

options.A: Nathu La

questions.explanation: Zoji La is located in the western Himalayas and connects the Kashmir Valley with the Ladakh region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Shipki La is associated with which river valley?

options.A: Sutlej Valley

questions.explanation: Shipki La is situated in Himachal Pradesh on the India–China border in the Sutlej valley region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a low saddle-like depression between mountain peaks?

options.A: Col

questions.explanation: A col is a low saddle-like depression between mountain peaks and may sometimes form a mountain pass.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following contains only mountain passes specifically listed in the PDF?

options.A: Zoji La, Banihal, Shipki La, Nathu La and Jelep La
options.B: Zoji La, Mariana Trench, Banihal and Nathu La
options.C: Chilika, Pulicat, Nathu La and Lipulekh
options.D: Rohtang Pass, Grand Canyon, Baralacha La and Kaveri

questions.explanation: The PDF lists Zoji La, Banihal, Shipki La, Nathu La, Jelep La, Rohtang Pass, Baralacha La, Khardung La, Lipulekh and Bomdi La as well-known Indian mountain passes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which condition produces a waterfall through differential erosion?

options.A: Hard rock overlying softer rock
options.B: Uniformly soft rock with no change in channel level

questions.explanation: When hard rock overlies softer rock, the softer rock erodes faster and the resistant layer forms a ledge, contributing to waterfall formation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which sequence correctly explains waterfall retreat caused by differential erosion?

options.A: Soft rock erosion → undercutting → collapse of resistant rock blocks → upstream retreat
options.B: Sand deposition → delta formation → ocean trench formation
options.C: Wind erosion → loess deposition → mountain uplift
options.D: Coral growth → lagoon formation → waterfall migration

questions.explanation: Softer rock is eroded faster, causing undercutting beneath the resistant layer. Rock blocks then collapse, allowing the waterfall to migrate upstream.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geological feature may produce a sudden change in a river-channel level and contribute to waterfall formation?

options.A: Fault or fracture

questions.explanation: Faults and fractures can create differences in elevation in a river channel and contribute to waterfall formation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following contains only waterfalls specifically named in the PDF?

options.A: Jog Falls, Kunchikal Falls, Dudhsagar Falls and Athirappilly Falls
options.B: Jog Falls, Niagara Falls, Victoria Falls and Angel Falls
options.C: Kunchikal Falls, Grand Canyon, Dudhsagar Falls and Chilika
options.D: Athirappilly Falls, Nathu La, Nohkalikai Falls and Banihal

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Jog Falls, Kunchikal Falls, Dudhsagar Falls, Athirappilly Falls, Nohkalikai Falls and Hogenakkal Falls as important Indian waterfalls.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a waterfall from rapids?

options.A: A waterfall has a marked steep or near-vertical drop, whereas rapids are turbulent stretches of fast-flowing water
options.B: Rapids always have a greater vertical drop than waterfalls
options.C: A waterfall is always a slow-moving stretch of water
options.D: Rapids and waterfalls are identical in every respect

questions.explanation: A waterfall has a marked steep or near-vertical drop. Rapids are turbulent stretches where water moves rapidly over an irregular or steep channel without one dominant vertical fall.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination helps maintain the steep walls of a canyon?

options.A: Tectonic uplift, resistant rock layers and limited lateral erosion

questions.explanation: Canyons are formed through prolonged river incision into bedrock. Tectonic uplift, resistant rock layers and limited lateral erosion can help maintain steep canyon walls.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the geological significance of the exposed rock layers in the Grand Canyon?

options.A: They record a long geological history
options.B: They demonstrate recent coral reef formation only
options.C: They indicate that the canyon is a coastal lagoon
options.D: They prove that the Colorado River is a glacial river

questions.explanation: The Grand Canyon is known for its immense scale and exposed sequence of rock layers, which record a long geological history. The Colorado River has cut deeply into the Colorado Plateau.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a gorge in Nepal mentioned in the PDF?

options.A: Kali Gandaki Gorge

questions.explanation: The Kali Gandaki Gorge in Nepal is a well-known example of a gorge. River gorges in the Himalayas are also mentioned.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which set of conditions is most favourable for the growth of a river delta?

options.A: Large sediment supply, shallow receiving basin, low wave and tidal energy, and sufficient accommodation space
options.B: No sediment supply, strong waves and very strong tidal currents
options.C: Only deep water and high wind speed
options.D: High sediment removal and absence of depositional space

questions.explanation: Delta growth is favoured by large sediment supply, a relatively shallow receiving basin, low wave and tidal energy and sufficient accommodation space. Strong waves or tides may reshape or limit delta growth.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the primary function of distributary channels in a delta?

options.A: To distribute water and sediment across the delta
options.B: To carry seawater towards mountain peaks
options.C: To transport sediments into ocean trenches

questions.explanation: Distributaries branch away from the main river near its mouth and distribute water and sediment across the delta.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about delta classification is correct?

options.A: Deltas can be classified by their shape or by the dominant processes controlling their development
options.B: All deltas are exclusively classified by water depth
options.D: Deltas cannot be classified into different types

questions.explanation: Delta classification can be based on shape or dominant processes. Common descriptive types include arcuate, bird's-foot, cuspate and tide-dominated or estuarine forms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which delta is associated with the Sundarbans?

options.A: Ganga–Brahmaputra Delta

questions.explanation: The Sundarbans are associated with the Ganga–Brahmaputra Delta system, which extends across India and Bangladesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a major environmental vulnerability of delta regions?

options.A: Flooding and salinity

questions.explanation: Deltas commonly contain fertile alluvial soils and abundant water, but they are vulnerable to floods and salinity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Ganga–Brahmaputra–Meghna delta system: 1. It is shared by India and Bangladesh. 2. It is identified in the PDF as the world's largest delta system. 3. It is associated with the Sundarbans. Which statements are correct?

options.A: 1 only

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. The Ganga–Brahmaputra–Meghna delta system is shared by India and Bangladesh, is the world's largest delta system and includes the Sundarbans region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An estuary is best described as which of the following?

options.A: A freshwater lake surrounded by mountains
options.B: A partly enclosed coastal water body where river water mixes with seawater
options.C: A deep depression in the ocean floor
options.D: A landform created exclusively by wind deposition

questions.explanation: An estuary is a partly enclosed coastal water body where freshwater from rivers mixes with seawater. It is generally influenced by tides and commonly contains brackish water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process commonly contributes to the formation of an estuary?

options.A: Flooding of a river valley due to rising sea level
options.D: Deposition of glacial ice on a mountain peak

questions.explanation: Estuaries commonly develop when rising sea levels flood existing river valleys, allowing seawater and freshwater to mix. Coastal processes can also create partly enclosed inlets.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is brackish water?

options.A: Water containing no dissolved salts
options.B: Water with salinity between freshwater and seawater
options.C: Water with a higher salinity than normal seawater

questions.explanation: Brackish water has a salinity level between that of freshwater and seawater. It is commonly found in estuaries and coastal lagoons.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which factor has a major influence on the water conditions of an estuary?

options.A: Tidal action

questions.explanation: Estuaries are strongly influenced by tides. Tidal movement affects water circulation, salinity, sediment transport and the mixing of freshwater with seawater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of estuarine water?

options.A: Its salinity remains permanently identical to freshwater
options.B: Its salinity can vary because of freshwater inflow and tidal seawater
options.D: It is unaffected by river discharge

questions.explanation: Estuarine salinity varies according to the amount of freshwater entering from rivers and the amount of seawater entering through tidal action.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important ecological function of estuaries?

options.A: Providing nursery habitats for fish and crustaceans
options.C: Producing permanent freshwater without river input

questions.explanation: Estuaries provide important nursery habitats for fish and crustaceans. They also support bird feeding grounds, nutrient cycling, sediment trapping and coastal protection.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of organisms particularly benefits from estuaries as nursery habitats?

options.A: Fish and crustaceans

questions.explanation: Estuaries provide productive nursery environments for fish and crustaceans, supporting their early growth and development.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following sets contains estuaries or estuarine systems identified in the study material as Indian examples?

options.A: Narmada, Tapi, Mandovi and Zuari

questions.explanation: Narmada, Tapi, Mandovi and Zuari are identified as Indian estuarine examples. Hooghly is also mentioned in the study material.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following rivers is mentioned as an example of an Indian estuarine system?

options.A: Narmada

questions.explanation: The Narmada is identified as an Indian estuarine example. The study material also lists Tapi, Mandovi, Zuari and Hooghly.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are estuaries common along parts of India's western coast?

options.A: The western coastal plain is relatively narrow and many rivers are short and swift
options.B: The western coast has no river systems
options.C: All rivers on the western coast form large deltas
options.D: The western coast is completely isolated from tidal influence

questions.explanation: The western coastal plain is relatively narrow. Rivers are often short and swift, and many river mouths experience tidal influence, favouring estuarine conditions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an estuary from a delta?

options.A: An estuary is mainly a tidal mixing zone, whereas a delta is mainly a depositional landform
options.B: An estuary is formed exclusively by wind, whereas a delta is formed by glaciers
options.C: Both are exclusively underwater volcanic features
options.D: A delta is always separated from the sea by a barrier island

questions.explanation: A delta forms mainly through sediment deposition at a river mouth and commonly contains distributaries. An estuary is a tidal river mouth or coastal inlet where freshwater and seawater mix. Some river mouths may display characteristics of both.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following statements about estuaries: 1. They receive freshwater and seawater. 2. They are influenced by tides. 3. Their salinity can vary. Which of the statements are correct?

options.A: 1 only

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. Estuaries receive river water and seawater, experience tidal influence and have variable salinity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified as an ecological or environmental function of estuaries in the study material?

options.A: Nutrient cycling

questions.explanation: Estuaries support nutrient cycling, sediment trapping, coastal protection, nursery habitats and feeding grounds. Mountain-range formation is unrelated to estuarine ecology.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a coastal lagoon?

options.A: A deep ocean trench formed by subduction
options.B: A shallow coastal water body partly or almost completely separated from the open sea
options.C: A river channel located in a mountain valley
options.D: A freshwater lake formed only by volcanic activity

questions.explanation: A lagoon is a shallow coastal water body separated partly or almost completely from the open sea by a barrier such as a sandbar, barrier island, reef or spit.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which coastal feature can act as a natural barrier separating a lagoon from the open sea?

options.A: Sandbar

questions.explanation: A sandbar can form a barrier between a coastal indentation and the open sea, helping enclose shallow water and create a lagoon.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which coastal processes commonly contribute to lagoon formation?

options.A: Wave action and longshore currents
options.C: Glacial movement in polar regions only

questions.explanation: Waves and longshore currents can build bars or spits across coastal indentations, enclosing shallow water and forming lagoons.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Besides sandbars and spits, which natural feature can enclose a lagoon?

options.A: Coral reef

questions.explanation: Coral reefs can form barriers around shallow coastal waters, enclosing lagoons.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a typical characteristic of lagoons?

options.A: They are generally shallow and may have restricted exchange with the sea
options.C: They are always completely isolated from every water source
options.D: They are formed exclusively by river erosion

questions.explanation: Lagoons are generally shallow coastal water bodies. Their exchange with the open sea may be restricted because of barriers, spits, sandbars or reefs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Depending on freshwater inflow and their connection with the sea, lagoon water may be:

options.A: Only freshwater
options.C: Freshwater, brackish water or saline water
options.D: Always completely free from dissolved salts

questions.explanation: The salinity of a lagoon depends on freshwater inflows and the degree of connection with the sea. Therefore, lagoon water may be freshwater, brackish or saline.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Chilika Lake is located in which Indian state?

options.A: Kerala

questions.explanation: Chilika Lake is a large brackish-water coastal lagoon located in Odisha.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Chilika Lake is separated from the Bay of Bengal mainly by which feature?

options.A: A barrier spit

questions.explanation: Chilika is separated from the Bay of Bengal by a barrier spit and remains connected to the sea through an inlet.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following lakes is located on the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu coast and is identified as a lagoon?

options.A: Pulicat Lake

questions.explanation: Pulicat Lake is a coastal lagoon located along the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu coast.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Vembanad Lake, an important coastal lagoon, is located in which state?

options.A: Odisha

questions.explanation: Vembanad Lake is an important lagoon located in Kerala.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the Indian lagoon with its state or coastal location?

options.A: Chilika — Odisha

questions.explanation: Chilika Lake is located in Odisha. Pulicat lies on the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu coast, while Vembanad is located in Kerala.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the principal difference between a lagoon and an estuary?

options.A: A lagoon is separated from the open sea by a barrier or reef, whereas an estuary is a tidal river mouth where freshwater and seawater mix
options.B: A lagoon is always deep, whereas an estuary is always dry
options.C: A lagoon forms only in deserts, whereas an estuary forms only in mountains

questions.explanation: A lagoon is a shallow coastal water body partly separated from the open sea by a barrier or reef. An estuary is a tidal river mouth or coastal inlet where freshwater and seawater mix. Both may contain brackish water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A sand dune is primarily formed through which geological process?

options.A: Wind deposition

questions.explanation: A sand dune is a hill or mound of loose sand formed through wind deposition. Dunes commonly occur in deserts and along coastlines.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination represents the three principal ways in which wind transports sand and sediment?

options.A: Saltation, surface creep and suspension

questions.explanation: Wind transports sediment through saltation, surface creep and suspension. These processes contribute to the movement and accumulation of sand that forms dunes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is saltation in the context of wind erosion and deposition?

options.A: The bouncing or hopping movement of sand-sized particles along the ground
options.B: The rolling of large rocks down a mountain slope
options.C: The chemical dissolution of minerals in seawater
options.D: The movement of glaciers over bedrock

questions.explanation: Saltation is the bouncing or hopping movement of sand-sized particles along the ground under the action of wind.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Surface creep refers to which type of sediment movement?

options.A: Rolling or sliding of larger sand grains along the ground
options.B: Suspension of fine particles high in the atmosphere
options.C: Movement of water through underground caves

questions.explanation: Surface creep is the rolling or sliding movement of relatively larger sand grains along the ground, often caused by impacts from saltating grains.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Under which condition is wind-blown sand most likely to accumulate and contribute to dune growth?

options.A: When wind speed decreases or an obstacle traps sand
options.C: When all sand particles dissolve in water
options.D: When tectonic plates move apart beneath the ocean

questions.explanation: Sand accumulates when wind loses some of its transporting capacity, such as when wind speed decreases or an obstacle traps moving particles.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly identifies the main parts of a typical sand dune?

options.A: Windward slope, crest and leeward slip face

questions.explanation: A typical dune has a windward slope, a crest and a steeper leeward slip face. These features are especially recognisable in simple transverse dunes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The steeper slope on the sheltered side of a typical sand dune is known as the:

options.A: Slip face

questions.explanation: The leeward side of a typical dune commonly forms a steeper slope called the slip face, where deposited sand moves downslope.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the angle of repose?

options.A: The steepest stable angle at which loose granular material can rest without sliding
options.B: The angle between two tectonic plates
options.C: The angle at which sunlight reaches the equator
options.D: The angle formed by the continental shelf and ocean surface

questions.explanation: The angle of repose is the steepest stable angle at which loose granular material can remain at rest without sliding. For dry sand, it is commonly around 30–35 degrees, depending on grain properties and moisture.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The commonly quoted angle of repose for dry sand is approximately:

options.A: 5–10 degrees

questions.explanation: The angle of repose of dry sand is commonly around 30–35 degrees. The exact value varies according to grain properties and moisture conditions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a major type of sand dune in the study material?

options.A: Barchan

questions.explanation: The major dune types listed are barchan, transverse, longitudinal, parabolic and star dunes. Arcuate is a type of delta, not a dune.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which sand dune is characteristically crescent-shaped?

options.A: Barchan dune

questions.explanation: A barchan is a crescent-shaped sand dune. It commonly forms where sand supply is limited and the wind direction is mainly one-way.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which direction do the horns of a typical barchan dune point?

options.A: Upwind

questions.explanation: The horns of a typical barchan dune point downwind. This is an important identifying characteristic of barchan dunes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Barchan dunes commonly develop under which combination of conditions?

options.A: Limited sand supply and mainly one-way wind
options.B: Abundant sand and completely random wind directions
options.D: High tidal energy and strong river deposition

questions.explanation: Barchan dunes commonly form where sand supply is limited and the prevailing wind direction is mainly consistent or one-way.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Transverse dunes are generally oriented in which direction in relation to the prevailing wind?

options.A: Broadly perpendicular
options.D: In a circular pattern around a river

questions.explanation: Transverse dunes form ridges oriented broadly perpendicular to the prevailing wind. They commonly occur where sand supply is abundant and wind direction is relatively consistent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which conditions are commonly associated with the formation of transverse dunes?

options.A: Abundant sand supply and relatively consistent wind direction
options.B: Limited sand supply and no wind
options.C: Variable tidal currents and river flooding

questions.explanation: Transverse dunes commonly develop where sand is abundant and the prevailing wind direction is relatively consistent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Longitudinal dunes are generally aligned in which direction?

options.A: Broadly parallel to the resultant wind direction
options.B: Broadly perpendicular to all wind directions

questions.explanation: Longitudinal dunes are long, narrow ridges aligned broadly parallel to the resultant wind direction. They may form under two dominant wind directions or more complex wind regimes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which dune is commonly U-shaped and has arms that generally point upwind?

options.A: Parabolic dune

questions.explanation: A parabolic dune is U-shaped. Its arms generally point upwind and are often anchored by vegetation. These dunes are common in coastal settings.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature commonly helps anchor the arms of parabolic dunes?

options.A: Vegetation

questions.explanation: The arms of parabolic dunes are often anchored by vegetation. These dunes commonly occur in coastal environments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of dune is characterised by multiple arms and is commonly associated with variable wind directions?

options.A: Star dune

questions.explanation: Star dunes have multiple arms and commonly form under variable wind directions. They are also associated with large sand supplies.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the dune type with its characteristic?

options.A: Barchan — Crescent-shaped with horns pointing downwind
options.B: Parabolic — Multiple arms formed by variable winds
options.D: Transverse — Long narrow ridges parallel to the resultant wind

questions.explanation: Barchan dunes are crescent-shaped and their horns point downwind. Parabolic dunes are U-shaped, star dunes have multiple arms, and longitudinal dunes are aligned broadly parallel to the resultant wind.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Indian region contains extensive sand dunes?

options.A: Thar Desert of Rajasthan

questions.explanation: The Thar Desert of Rajasthan contains extensive sand dunes. Coastal dune systems are also found along parts of India's coastline.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between active and stabilised sand dunes?

options.A: Active dunes are mobile under wind action, whereas stabilised dunes are held in place by factors such as vegetation or moisture
options.B: Active dunes contain only silt, whereas stabilised dunes contain only clay
options.C: Active dunes occur only underwater, whereas stabilised dunes occur only on mountains
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: Active dunes move under wind action. Stabilised dunes are held in place partly by vegetation, moisture, surface crusts or human intervention.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is loess?

options.A: A widespread deposit of wind-blown silt
options.B: A volcanic rock formed from cooled lava
options.D: A coastal landform made entirely of coral

questions.explanation: Loess is a widespread deposit of wind-blown silt. It is usually unstratified, commonly pale yellow or buff, and contains a high proportion of silt-sized particles.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which particle size forms the dominant component of loess deposits?

options.A: Silt-sized particles

questions.explanation: Loess consists mainly of wind-blown silt-sized particles. It is generally fine-grained and commonly forms extensive deposits over broad areas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following can provide fine sediment that is later transported by wind to form loess deposits?

options.A: Glacial grinding, desert weathering and drying of floodplains

questions.explanation: Fine sediment for loess can originate through glacial grinding, desert weathering, floodplain drying and other processes. Wind subsequently transports and deposits the fine material over broad areas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which colour is commonly associated with loess deposits?

options.A: Pale yellow or buff

questions.explanation: Loess is commonly pale yellow or buff in colour. It is a widespread deposit of wind-blown silt.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which description most accurately represents the usual structure of loess deposits?

options.A: Widespread and usually unstratified deposits
options.B: Regularly layered deposits of large boulders
options.C: Deeply folded layers of marine limestone
options.D: Alternating layers of volcanic lava and ash exclusively

questions.explanation: Loess is generally a widespread, usually unstratified deposit of wind-blown silt. It may be weakly stratified in some settings.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which physical property is commonly associated with loess?

options.A: Porous nature

questions.explanation: Loess is commonly porous and fine-grained. It may form steep-sided vertical bluffs and is susceptible to erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination correctly describes important characteristics of loess?

options.A: Fine-grained, porous and commonly weakly stratified or unstratified
options.C: Entirely composed of large rounded boulders
options.D: Always formed beneath deep ocean water

questions.explanation: Loess is commonly fine-grained and porous. Its deposits are usually unstratified or weakly stratified and may form steep-sided bluffs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why can loess deposits develop fertile soils?

options.A: They commonly contain abundant silt and mineral nutrients and can retain moisture
options.B: They consist entirely of dissolved salts

questions.explanation: Loess soils can be fertile because they commonly contain abundant silt and mineral nutrients and can retain moisture. Actual fertility also depends on climate, soil development and land management.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about the fertility of loess soils is most accurate?

options.A: All loess soils are equally fertile under every climatic condition
options.B: Loess soils can be fertile, but their fertility depends on several environmental and management factors
options.C: Loess soils are always infertile because they contain no minerals
options.D: Loess fertility depends exclusively on ocean tides

questions.explanation: Although loess commonly contains mineral nutrients and moisture-retaining silt, soil fertility varies with climate, soil development and land management.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which region is particularly famous for extensive loess deposits?

options.A: Loess Plateau of northern China

questions.explanation: The Loess Plateau of northern China is the best-known large region of extensive loess deposits.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Apart from northern China, which set of regions is identified as containing extensive loess deposits?

options.A: Parts of Europe, Central Asia, North America and Argentina
options.D: Only the islands of the Indian Ocean

questions.explanation: Extensive loess deposits occur in parts of Europe, Central Asia, North America and Argentina, in addition to the well-known Loess Plateau of northern China.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Loess Plateau is located in which country?

options.A: China

questions.explanation: The Loess Plateau is a large region of thick wind-blown silt deposits in north-central China.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which landform process has deeply dissected the Loess Plateau of northern China?

options.A: Gully erosion

questions.explanation: The Loess Plateau is deeply dissected by gullies and has historically experienced severe soil erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which environmental problem has historically affected the Loess Plateau?

options.A: Severe soil erosion

questions.explanation: The Loess Plateau has historically been affected by severe soil erosion. Its thick deposits are deeply dissected by gullies.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which property makes loess deposits particularly vulnerable to erosion?

options.A: Their fine-grained and relatively weakly consolidated nature
options.B: Their complete composition of solid metallic minerals
options.C: Their permanent protection beneath coral reefs
options.D: Their formation exclusively from massive granite blocks

questions.explanation: Loess is fine-grained and commonly porous. Although it can support fertile soils, it may be highly susceptible to erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature may develop in thick loess deposits as a result of erosion?

options.A: Gullies

questions.explanation: Thick loess deposits can be deeply dissected by gullies. The Loess Plateau of northern China is a prominent example.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes loess from sand dunes?

options.A: Loess is mainly wind-deposited silt, whereas dunes are mainly mounds or ridges of wind-deposited sand
options.B: Loess is formed only by marine deposition, whereas dunes are formed only by river erosion
options.C: Both consist exclusively of large boulders
options.D: Dunes are made of silt blankets, whereas loess consists of coral sand

questions.explanation: Loess consists mainly of wind-deposited silt spread over broad areas. Sand dunes are mounds or ridges formed mainly by the accumulation of wind-deposited sand.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following statements about loess: 1. It is mainly composed of wind-blown silt. 2. It is commonly porous. 3. It may form steep-sided bluffs. Which statements are correct?

options.A: 1 only

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. Loess is a fine-grained wind-blown silt deposit that is commonly porous and may form steep-sided vertical bluffs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about major loess deposits in India is supported by the study material?

options.A: The Thar Desert is identified as India's major loess region
options.B: No major Indian loess region is commonly emphasised in standard school geography
options.C: The Sundarbans are identified as the world's largest loess deposit
options.D: The Western Ghats are identified as a major global loess plateau

questions.explanation: The study material notes that no major Indian loess region is commonly emphasised in standard school geography, while northern China is the classic world example.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which ocean-floor feature represents the shallow, gently sloping submerged extension of a continent?

options.A: Continental shelf

questions.explanation: The continental shelf is the shallow, gently sloping submerged extension of a continent. It extends from the shoreline to the shelf break.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature forms the steep descent from the continental shelf towards the deep ocean?

options.A: Continental slope

questions.explanation: The continental slope begins beyond the shelf break and descends relatively steeply towards the deep-ocean floor or continental rise.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature is primarily a sediment-built zone at the foot of many continental slopes?

options.A: Continental rise

questions.explanation: The continental rise is a relatively gentle sediment accumulation zone at the base of many continental slopes. It is often well developed along passive continental margins.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which ocean-floor feature is characterised by an extensive and extremely flat surface?

options.A: Abyssal plain

questions.explanation: An abyssal plain is an extensive, very flat region of the deep-ocean floor. Sediment accumulation helps smooth underlying ocean-floor relief.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A long, narrow and extremely deep depression on the ocean floor is known as a:

options.A: Trench

questions.explanation: Ocean trenches are long, narrow and extremely deep depressions on the ocean floor. They are commonly associated with subduction zones.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature is a submarine mountain chain commonly associated with divergent plate boundaries?

options.A: Mid-ocean ridge

questions.explanation: Mid-ocean ridges are submarine mountain chains that occur mainly at divergent plate boundaries, where new oceanic crust forms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pair of ocean-floor features is correctly matched with its principal geological setting?

options.A: Mid-ocean ridge — Divergent boundary; Ocean trench — Convergent subduction boundary
options.B: Mid-ocean ridge — Subduction zone; Ocean trench — Divergent boundary

questions.explanation: Mid-ocean ridges are mainly associated with divergent plate boundaries, while ocean trenches are associated with convergent plate boundaries where subduction occurs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature commonly marks the transition between the shallow continental shelf and the steeper continental slope?

options.A: Shelf break

questions.explanation: The shelf break is the point or zone where the gently sloping continental shelf transitions into the steeper continental slope.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly explains why the continental rise may be absent in some regions?

options.A: It may be absent near ocean trenches
options.B: It is always absent near passive margins
options.C: It forms only above mountain peaks
options.D: It is replaced by sand dunes in every ocean basin

questions.explanation: The continental rise is a sediment accumulation zone at the foot of many continental slopes, but it may be absent near trenches.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the coastal landform with its dominant process?

options.A: Delta — River-mouth sediment deposition

questions.explanation: A delta is formed mainly by sediment accumulation when a river enters a standing body of water and loses transport capacity. The other options describe incorrect processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature is most directly associated with a tidal mixing zone between river water and seawater?

options.A: Estuary

questions.explanation: An estuary is a tidal river mouth or coastal inlet where freshwater and seawater mix, commonly producing brackish water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature is most directly associated with a shallow coastal water body partly enclosed by a sandbar, spit or reef?

options.A: Lagoon

questions.explanation: A lagoon is a shallow coastal water body partly or almost completely separated from the open sea by a barrier such as a sandbar, barrier island, reef or spit.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched according to the material's distinction between wind-deposited landforms?

options.A: Sand dune — Sand accumulation; Loess — Silt accumulation
options.B: Sand dune — Silt accumulation; Loess — Sand accumulation

questions.explanation: Sand dunes are formed mainly from wind-deposited sand, whereas loess consists mainly of wind-blown silt.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about canyons and gorges is most consistent with the study material?

options.A: Both are steep-sided valleys, and their distinction is mainly based on scale and regional usage
options.B: A canyon is always a coastal lagoon, whereas a gorge is an ocean trench
options.C: A gorge is always wider than every canyon
options.D: The two terms have a universally fixed scientific boundary

questions.explanation: Canyons and gorges are both steep-sided valleys. Canyon often describes a very large or extensive valley, while gorge often describes a narrower valley. Usage varies by region, and there is no strict universal boundary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river is associated with Jog Falls in Karnataka?

options.A: Sharavathi

questions.explanation: Jog Falls is located on the Sharavathi River in Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Kunchikal Falls is identified in the study material as being located in which state?

options.A: Karnataka

questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls is listed among the important Indian waterfall examples in Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Dudhsagar Falls is associated with which river system?

options.A: Mandovi

questions.explanation: Dudhsagar Falls is associated with the Mandovi river system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following sets contains only Indian rivers whose deltas are listed in the study material?

options.A: Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri

questions.explanation: The Indian deltas listed include those of the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri, along with the Ganga–Brahmaputra Delta.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only Indian estuarine examples listed in the study material?

options.A: Narmada, Tapi, Mandovi and Zuari

questions.explanation: Narmada, Tapi, Mandovi and Zuari are listed as Indian estuarine examples. The second group contains rivers associated with important Indian deltas, while the third contains lake names.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct combination of Indian coastal lagoons mentioned in the study material?

options.A: Chilika, Pulicat and Vembanad

questions.explanation: Chilika, Pulicat and Vembanad are the important Indian lagoons identified in the study material.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Indian geographical region is associated with extensive sand dune systems?

options.A: Thar Desert

questions.explanation: The Thar Desert of Rajasthan contains extensive sand dunes. Coastal dune systems also occur along parts of India's coastline.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Indian examples of deltas and estuaries listed in the study material?

options.A: Godavari and Krishna are listed as delta examples, while Narmada and Tapi are listed as estuarine examples
options.B: Narmada and Tapi are listed as major delta examples, while Godavari and Krishna are listed as estuaries
options.C: Chilika and Pulicat are listed as mountain passes
options.D: Sharavathi and Mandovi are listed as continental shelves

questions.explanation: Godavari and Krishna are among the Indian rivers associated with deltas in the material. Narmada and Tapi are listed among the estuarine examples.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about the continental shelf is correct?

options.A: It is part of the submerged continental margin
options.B: It is the deepest part of the ocean
options.C: It is always a narrow volcanic ridge
options.D: It is formed only by wind deposition

questions.explanation: The continental shelf is the shallow, submerged extension of a continent. It should not be confused with the deep-ocean floor.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the gradients of the continental shelf and continental slope?

options.A: The continental shelf is gently sloping, while the continental slope is relatively steep
options.B: The continental shelf is steeper than the continental slope
options.C: Both have exactly the same gradient everywhere
options.D: The continental shelf is vertical, while the slope is horizontal

questions.explanation: The continental shelf has a gentle gradient, whereas the continental slope is the relatively steep descent beyond the shelf break.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between the Mariana Trench and Challenger Deep?

options.A: Challenger Deep is the deepest surveyed area within the Mariana Trench
options.B: The Mariana Trench is located inside Challenger Deep
options.C: Both are names for mid-ocean ridges
options.D: Challenger Deep is a continental shelf

questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench is the deepest known ocean trench, while Challenger Deep is its deepest surveyed area. These two terms should not be treated as identical geographical features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about mountain passes is correct?

options.A: A mountain pass is a relatively low route through a mountain range
options.B: A mountain pass is always the highest peak in a mountain range
options.C: A mountain pass is a deep-ocean depression
options.D: A mountain pass is a depositional feature formed by river sediment

questions.explanation: A mountain pass is a relatively low route through a mountain range that can provide a route for movement across mountainous terrain. It is not a mountain peak.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified as a possible process or setting involved in waterfall formation?

options.A: Differential erosion
options.D: Wind-blown silt deposition as the defining process

questions.explanation: Waterfalls may form through differential erosion, faulting, glaciation or at plateau edges. Wind-blown silt deposition is associated with loess, not the defining formation of waterfalls.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which condition may limit or reshape the growth of a river delta?

options.A: Strong wave and tidal energy
options.C: Permanent lack of water in the receiving basin

questions.explanation: Delta formation is favoured by sediment deposition, but strong waves and tides can redistribute sediments and reshape or limit delta growth.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes abyssal plains from ocean trenches?

options.A: Abyssal plains are broad and flat, whereas trenches are narrow and extremely deep
options.B: Abyssal plains are narrow depressions, whereas trenches are broad flat surfaces
options.C: Both are shallow parts of the continental shelf

questions.explanation: Abyssal plains are extensive, relatively flat deep-ocean regions. Ocean trenches are long, narrow and extremely deep depressions, commonly associated with subduction zones.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. New oceanic crust forms at mid-ocean ridges. 2. Ocean trenches are associated with subduction zones. 3. Continental rises are commonly formed by sediment accumulation. Which statements are correct?

options.A: 1 only

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. Mid-ocean ridges are sites of new oceanic crust formation, trenches are associated with subduction, and continental rises develop through sediment accumulation at the foot of many continental slopes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following statements about coastal landforms: 1. Deltas are associated with river-mouth sediment deposition. 2. Estuaries are influenced by tides. 3. Lagoons are partly separated from the open sea by barriers or reefs. Which statements are correct?

options.A: 1 only

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct and represent the principal distinctions among deltas, estuaries and lagoons described in the study material.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the simplified order of major continental-margin features from the coast towards the deep ocean?

options.A: Continental shelf → Continental slope → Continental rise → Deep-ocean basin
options.B: Continental slope → Continental shelf → Ocean trench → Continental rise
options.C: Abyssal plain → Continental shelf → Continental rise → Continental slope
options.D: Ocean trench → Continental shelf → Continental slope → Continental rise

questions.explanation: The simplified continental-margin sequence proceeds from the continental shelf to the continental slope, then to the continental rise where developed, and finally towards the deep-ocean basin.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which option correctly matches all four geographical features with their principal descriptions?

options.A: Estuary — Tidal freshwater-seawater mixing; Lagoon — Barrier-separated coastal water; Loess — Wind-blown silt; Barchan — Crescent-shaped dune
options.B: Estuary — Wind-blown silt; Lagoon — Ocean trench; Loess — River delta; Barchan — Mountain pass
options.C: Estuary — Submarine ridge; Lagoon — Deep canyon; Loess — Coral reef; Barchan — Abyssal plain
options.D: Estuary — Mountain pass; Lagoon — Continental slope; Loess — Ocean trench; Barchan — River distributary

questions.explanation: An estuary is a tidal mixing zone, a lagoon is partly separated from the sea by a barrier, loess is wind-blown silt, and a barchan is a crescent-shaped sand dune.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which option correctly matches the major geographical feature with its Indian example?

options.A: Waterfall — Jog Falls; Lagoon — Chilika Lake; Estuary — Narmada; Delta — Mahanadi
options.B: Waterfall — Chilika Lake; Lagoon — Jog Falls; Estuary — Mahanadi; Delta — Narmada
options.C: Waterfall — Narmada; Lagoon — Mahanadi; Estuary — Chilika Lake; Delta — Jog Falls
options.D: Waterfall — Mahanadi; Lagoon — Narmada; Estuary — Jog Falls; Delta — Chilika Lake

questions.explanation: Jog Falls is a waterfall on the Sharavathi River in Karnataka. Chilika is a coastal lagoon in Odisha. Narmada is listed as an estuarine example, and Mahanadi is associated with a major Indian delta.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mountain pass is located in Sikkim on the India–China border?

options.A: Nathu La

questions.explanation: Nathu La is located in Sikkim on the India–China border and forms part of a historic trade route.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Zoji La connects which two geographical regions?

options.A: Kashmir Valley and Ladakh

questions.explanation: Zoji La is located in the western Himalayas and connects the Kashmir Valley with the Ladakh region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Shipki La is located in which Indian state?

options.A: Himachal Pradesh

questions.explanation: Shipki La is located in Himachal Pradesh, on the India–China border, in the Sutlej Valley region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mountain pass is associated with the Sutlej Valley region and the India–China border?

options.A: Shipki La

questions.explanation: Shipki La is situated in Himachal Pradesh in the Sutlej Valley region, along the India–China border.
